#### Interaction states

Use this example for selecting a date. Adjust disabled, read-only, error feedback and compare the component with the same data. The controls remain available to restore editing; error appearance alone does not run validation.

</details>

Example source: src/date/example/demos/state-lab.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { reactive as __demoReactive, ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('2026-10-23')
const __demoState = __demoReactive({ disabled: false, readonly: false, error: false })
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-checkbox v-model="__demoState['disabled']">disabled</mp-checkbox>
      <mp-checkbox v-model="__demoState['readonly']">readonly</mp-checkbox>
      <mp-checkbox v-model="__demoState['error']">error</mp-checkbox>
    </mp-space>
    <mp-date v-model="value" value-format="YYYY-MM-DD" v-bind="__demoState"></mp-date>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Rejected controlled close

The parent may reject `update:open(false)` and keep the panel open. An equal controlled-model echo does not reset the confirmed state, so repeated confirmation neither submits nor requests another close. A new date starts a new transaction. The demo shows the model, commit count, and close-request count.

Example source: src/date/example/demos/en-US/rejected-close.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('2026-09-22')
const open = ref(false)
const closeRequests = ref(0)
const commits = ref(0)

function requestOpen(next) {
  if (next) {
    open.value = true
  } else {
    closeRequests.value++
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="12px">
    <p>
      The parent rejects close requests. A new date starts a new confirmation; repeated confirmation does not submit
      twice.
    </p>
    <mp-date v-model="value" :open="open" panel-type="calendar" @update:open="requestOpen" @change="commits++" />
    <span data-test="date-transaction-state"
      >Value: {{ value }}; commits: {{ commits }}; rejected closes: {{ closeRequests }}</span
    >
    <mp-button @click="open = false">Allow close</mp-button>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Field viewport and shortcut events

Configure `pickerValue`, `defaultPickerValue` and shortcuts through nested `datePickerProps` / `dateRangePickerProps`; listeners inside nested objects are filtered. Listen on the field and update the nested viewport. Controlled rejection keeps the previous month; navigation does not select or commit. A valid shortcut chooses a draft under the existing confirmation policy.

| Event | Description | Parameters |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `update:picker-value` | Request calendar viewport update | value: DateSelection |
| `picker-value-change` | Viewport request and formatted payload | value, date(s), formatted text(s) |
| `select-shortcut` | Accepted shortcut object | shortcut: DateShortcut |

Example source: src/date/example/demos/en-US/field-panel-tools.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { DateShortcut } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const selected = ref('2025-01-15')
const viewport = ref('2025-01-01')
const acceptNavigation = ref(true)
const notice = ref('')
const shortcutNotice = ref('')
const shortcuts: DateShortcut[] = [
  { label: 'Next month', value: '2025-02-15' },
  { label: 'Disabled', value: '2025-03-01', disabled: true },
]
function navigate(value: unknown) {
  if (acceptNavigation.value && typeof value === 'string') {
    viewport.value = value
  }
}
function observe(_value: unknown, _dates: unknown, texts: unknown) {
  notice.value = String(texts)
}
function choose(shortcut: DateShortcut) {
  shortcutNotice.value = String(shortcut.label)
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-checkbox v-model="acceptNavigation">Accept viewport requests</mp-checkbox>
  <mp-date
    v-model="selected"
    panel-type="calendar"
    :input-editable="false"
    format="DD/MM/YYYY"
    :date-picker-props="{ pickerValue: viewport, shortcuts }"
    @update:picker-value="navigate"
    @picker-value-change="observe"
    @select-shortcut="choose"
  />
  <p>Selected model: {{ selected }}；Controlled viewport: {{ viewport }}</p>
  <p>Viewport event: {{ notice }}；Shortcut event: {{ shortcutNotice }}</p>
  <p>
    Navigation does not change selection. Rejected requests keep the previous viewport. Shortcuts select a draft;
    Confirm commits it.
  </p>
</template>
```

### Root-only presentation selection

`Date` / `DateRange` fields select their content through root `panel-type`; standalone date panels use root `presentation`. Both fields default to `calendar` content; standalone date panels default to `calendarPicker`. Field `DatePickerOptions` / `DateRangePickerOptions` do not accept root-owned `presentation`; untyped nested selectors are filtered at runtime. Week start, viewport, shortcuts and valid appearance remain configurable. Single roots support picker/calendar/calendarPicker; ranges support picker/calendar/calendarPicker. Cedar only implements its desktop calendar and does not expose empty mobile modes.

### Reactive first weekday

`dayStartOfWeek` updates the calendar headers and date columns together without changing the selected value or submitting a draft. Use the root prop on pure panels; on fields configure `datePickerProps` / `dateRangePickerProps`. The wheel view does not use weekday columns.

### Dynamic date limits

Updating or removing `min` / `max` changes selectable dates, not the existing model or draft. In Maple calendar views, day/month/year navigation availability is derived from the current viewport and both limits; removing one limit restores only that side. A released bound does not trigger selection or submission.

### Editing and confirmation

`edit-mode` inherits from field > FormItem > Form and defaults to `popup`. Supported values are `direct / popup`. Inline keeps the existing control behavior. Overlay editing uses a Cell reference and an isolated draft; only confirmation updates v-model. Cancel, reset and enabling readPretty discard the draft.

Maple edit-mode="popup" opens the editor by clicking the value area; direct edits directly. readPretty is independent reading mode, separate from readonly/disabled.

`before-commit(value, { previousValue, signal })` can reject an overlay save. FormItem validates the candidate first and keeps the editor open on failure. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. Use `#read="{ value, text }"` to customize display. See the full field comparison in Form.

Direct editing keeps the existing date/time confirmation policy. In popup, the inner pure panel hides its toolbar and the host owns the single confirmation boundary. Standalone DatePicker, DateRangePicker, TimePicker and TimeRangePicker retain their panel API and confirmation behavior. On fields, use `panel-type` to choose calendar/picker content; `edit-mode` controls the field container. Standalone date pickers use `presentation` for panel content; time pickers follow their panel APIs.

Standalone, inline and popup editors share the same layout. The calendar has a preferred width of 265px with extra space for a half-hour quick time Picker when time is enabled; narrow screens fit the available width. The footer displays the date, time and a clock/calendar toggle. Explicit `presentation="picker"` preserves date wheels. The panel retains standalone confirmation and actions ownership.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

### Shared mobile panel style

Single date, date-time and time panels omit the top summary in standalone panels and field editors. Date-time editors retain the current date/time and view switch at the bottom. Range summaries remain visible and highlight the active endpoint.

The calendar's central heading is a keyboard-accessible button with a dropdown indicator: activate it to choose months, then years. Use the footer calendar button to return to the date view without committing a value.


# Time zones and calendar views

`time-zone` accepts an IANA zone such as `America/New_York`. Dates and millisecond timestamps represent instants; strings represent civil time in that zone. Display, text entry, limits, shortcuts and disabled rules share this protocol. Event Dates remain actual instants. Omit the prop for existing host-local behavior. DST gaps are rejected, folds choose the earlier instant, and invalid zones block submission.

`interactive-mode` is `page` by default. `scroll` shows months between the limits with `use-virtual-scroll` enabled by default; without limits, the initial viewport has a one-year window on each side. `line` separates weekday headings from a row of dates, reuses round date selection, and labels the visible week with its date range. Previous/next buttons move by one week. Navigation never commits a field draft. Day-precision date-time uses these views together with the existing quick-time and detailed wheels. Range summaries, endpoint locks, reversed-range feedback and confirmation remain owned by the existing field transaction. Non-day precision retains its existing renderer.

Virtual months have equal height and six week rows. Customize `--mp-date-calendar-scroll-height`, `--mp-date-calendar-month-height`, `--mp-date-calendar-row-height` and `--mp-date-calendar-line-height` together. Existing calendar color tokens cover both brands and light/dark modes. Disabling virtualization renders the entire range.

### Shared field and commit protocol

Date / DateRange allow manual entry by default; input-editable can disable it. Time manual entry is controlled by inputEditable. Panels edit a draft and commit on confirmation; cancellation or external closing leaves the value unchanged. Clearing commits an empty value immediately and closes the panel. Date and time ranges display two inputs, retaining a next-day indicator for overnight time ranges.

Example source: src/date/example/demos/en-US/field-protocol.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const disabled = ref(false)
const date = ref('2026-09-22')
const dateRange = ref(['2026-09-22', '2026-09-24'])
const time = ref('09:00')
const timeRange = ref(['23:00', '01:00'])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <p>
      Range fields: tap the right input to edit the end. Switching sides only changes the draft; Confirm commits it.
    </p>
    <span>Disable fields</span>
    <mp-switch v-model="disabled" aria-label="Disable fields" />
    <mp-date v-model="date" :disabled="disabled" clearable placeholder="Date" />
    <mp-date-range v-model="dateRange" :disabled="disabled" clearable placeholder="Date range" />
    <mp-time v-model="time" format="HH:mm" :disabled="disabled" clearable placeholder="Time" />
    <mp-time-range
      v-model="timeRange"
      format="HH:mm"
      :disabled="disabled"
      clearable
      show-next-day
      placeholder="Time range"
    />
    <p>Date：{{ date || 'Empty' }}；Date range：{{ dateRange }}</p>
    <p>Time：{{ time || 'Empty' }}；Time range：{{ timeRange }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Intro

Date selection **panel**. DatePicker demos are included on this page; there is no separate date-picker documentation route. See the range documentation for [`DateRangePicker`](#/en-US/date-range). Form fields: [`Date`](#/en-US/date) / [`DateRange`](#/en-US/date-range).

The embedded panel example explicitly sets `disable-confirm=false`: selecting a date edits the draft; the committed value updates only after confirmation. Changing week start or removing bounds does not commit a value. Restoring bounds does not clear the existing model; an out-of-bounds draft cannot be confirmed until a valid date is selected.

Calendar arrows have localized accessible names: previous/next month in the day panel, year in the month panel, and years in the year list. They use global Locale, allow local LocaleProvider overrides, and fall back to the global translation for missing navigation keys. Boundaries still disable navigation; changing the preview does not commit a date.

### Field and embedded panel

Fields own input and popup state; panels embed directly. day-start-of-week accepts integer 0–6 (Sunday=0), with reactive range-calendar updates. Nested Options configure presentation only, not values, formats, bounds or disabled rules.

Example source: src/date/example/demos/en-US/entry-boundary.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { DateSelection } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const limited = ref(true)
const fieldValue = ref<DateSelection>('2025-02-12')
const panelValue = ref<DateSelection>('2025-02-12')
const week = ref<0 | 1 | 6>(1)
const presentation = ref<'picker' | 'calendar'>('calendar')
</script>

<template>
  <div class="entry-demo">
    <p>Limit selectable dates to February 2025; removing limits does not change the existing selection.</p>
    <mp-button @click="limited = !limited">{{ limited ? 'Remove limits' : 'Apply limits' }}</mp-button>
    <p>The root presentation selects the view. Nested date-picker-props only configures calendar appearance.</p>
    <mp-space>
      <mp-button @click="presentation = 'picker'">Wheel</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="presentation = 'calendar'">Calendar</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p>Changing the first weekday updates both headers and date columns, without changing the selection.</p>
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="week = 0">Sunday first</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="week = 1">Monday first</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="week = 6">Saturday first</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <div>
      <p>Field: input and popup ownership; use date-picker-props for presentation.</p>
      <mp-date
        v-model="fieldValue"
        :min="limited ? '2025-02-01' : undefined"
        :max="limited ? '2025-02-28' : undefined"
        :panel-type="presentation"
        :date-picker-props="{ dayStartOfWeek: week }"
        placeholder="Select date"
      />
    </div>
    <div>
      <p>Panel: embedded directly, without open or popup-container.</p>
      <mp-date-picker
        v-model="panelValue"
        :min="limited ? '2025-02-01' : undefined"
        :max="limited ? '2025-02-28' : undefined"
        :presentation="presentation"
        :day-start-of-week="week"
        :disable-confirm="false"
      />
      <p>Committed: {{ panelValue }}</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.entry-demo {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 16px;
}
</style>
```

### Typed passthrough configuration

Use `DatePopupOptions` from `@maple-design/ui-vue` for opt-in boundary checking. Published wide prop types and runtime precedence remain unchanged. Visibility, disabled state and owned updates belong to the host. Top-level popupContainer wins when defined (including false), otherwise the existing nested fallback applies. Select/Cascader keep nested overrides for existing presentation defaults, including unmountOnClose. Date/DateRange filter owned state, rules and listeners; their interaction/offset settings and mobile unmountOnClose are fixed by the renderer.

Example source: src/date/example/demos/passthrough-options.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { DatePopupOptions } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const open = ref(false)
const popupOptions: DatePopupOptions = { placement: 'top-start', popupTranslate: [0, -8], popupContainer: false }
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" fill>
    <mp-button @click="open = !open">{{ open ? '关闭面板' : '打开面板' }}</mp-button>
    <mp-date v-model:open="open" edit-mode="direct" :popup-props="popupOptions" aria-label="透传配置示例" />
    <p role="status">顶层 open：{{ open }}；嵌套配置：向上展开并调整偏移。</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

DST gaps, including half-hour transitions, disable only nonexistent times. New civil selections use the earlier fold occurrence. Existing Date/timestamp values preserve their occurrence and hidden milliseconds through zone changes, unchanged confirmation and edits to the opposite endpoint. Strings cannot encode which fold occurrence was intended.

### Copying and editing

Use open-trigger-target to control pointer opening independently. In icon mode, clicking, focusing and typing do not automatically open the panel. input-editable / filterable still controls editing or search. The suffix button, explicit keyboard commands and controlled open can open it.

Example source: src/date/example/demos/open-trigger-target.vue

```vue
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-radio-group
      v-model="target"
      :options="[
        { label: '整个字段', value: 'field' },
        { label: '仅右侧图标', value: 'icon' },
      ]"
    />
    <label><mp-switch v-model="editable" /> 允许编辑 / 搜索</label>
    <mp-date v-model="value" edit-mode="direct" :open-trigger-target="target" :input-editable="editable" />
    <p>关闭编辑后，可以复制已有文本；仅图标模式下编辑不会展开。</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const target = ref<'field' | 'icon'>('icon')
const editable = ref(true)
const value = ref('2026-10-27')
</script>
```

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Calendar dates, months and years follow reading order; navigation icons mirror, while date values keep their meaning. In paged grids, Left/Right moves focus visually, Up/Down moves one row, and Home/End moves to the row boundary, skipping disabled items. Focus navigation does not select; Enter/Space keeps the existing selection behavior. Navigation is bounded by the displayed grid. Explicit `shortcuts-position="left|right"` remains physical; `bottom` stays below. Field popovers inherit their source direction.

## Triggers and positioning

### Popup placement

The Date field prefers bottom-start below its input. Override the preferred side through popupProps.placement only when needed; the underlying Trigger positions it, not Popup or Popover. DatePicker is a standalone date panel with no input anchor. Configure popup placement on the Date field.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

## Usage notes

### Panel configuration

DatePicker and DateRangePicker provide standalone date selection. Use `show-current` for current-date highlighting and `picker-value` or `default-picker-value` for the displayed date.

Use showCurrent for current-date highlighting, showNowButton for selecting now, pickerValue/defaultPickerValue for the viewport, and min/max/disabledDate for selectable-value constraints. Existing field lists, abbreviation, wheel settings, appearance and actual panel capabilities remain available. loading-icon is not wired to a public panel or date-field slot and is not an available capability.


<!-- date-contract:start -->

### Values and formats

DateValue is string, number or native Date. Numbers are timestamps and 0 is not empty; modelValue=null is explicitly empty. Ranges retain broad arrays and incomplete endpoints rather than forcing a tuple; commits still validate completeness and validity. Maple general DatePicker/Date multiple selection does not widen Cedar single-value Props.

Tables list actual public properties. Inherited/precision-derived defaults describe resolved behavior; raw Props can be undefined. format controls display/text input and valueFormat controls the model protocol. Week/quarter display labels differ from model formats; function format has no reverse parser for text input.

Bounds are inclusive. Invalid supplied bounds block confirmation instead of being treated as omitted. Tightening rules does not clear the business model. disabledDate/disabledTime are explicit validation callbacks rather than asynchronous event tasks; time callbacks return disabled lists through DateDisabledTime.

### Date Slots / Methods

Field default replaces the trigger; prefix/selected/suffix replace content, and ranges also support separator. Preserve names, endpoint distinctions and keyboard access when replacing native controls. read receives value/text, suffix-icon receives focus/popupOpen, and clear-icon receives guarded clear(event?), respecting emptyValue and disabled/readonly guards.

actions receives confirm/disabled/selectNow/nowDisabled, with both actions returning void. It has no Time-panel canConfirm/value arguments. disabled=true prevents confirmation. Standalone panels can replace the action region; the outer editing shell owns final saving in hosted editing, while the panel contributes auxiliary actions. Panel confirm is not the outer-save method.

Now capabilities follow the actual panel: Cedar single panels support it, while Cedar range panels have no now action. Maple range panels stage now for the active endpoint, preserve the other endpoint and still require confirmation. The presence of selectNow in scope does not imply every mode supports the action.

Cedar cell customizes a calendar cell with date and, for ranges, type=start/end; extra adds content. Maple Date/DatePicker page-calendar summaries support year({year}), month({year,month}), date({week,year,month,date}), range({choose}) and multiple({choose}) according to mode. Maple DateRange/DateRangePicker do not forward these single-panel summary slots, nor do scroll/line viewports promise them.

loading-icon is not wired to date fields or pure panels and is not available merely because the underlying decorator supports it. Field focus(index?)/blur() delegate to real controls. Cedar/direct-field blur closes the field popup; Maple range persistent-reference blur only clears its focus, without pretending to close the outer Drawer. Pure panels expose no focus/blur methods.

### Presentation configuration and ranges

datePickerProps/dateRangePickerProps configure presentation without overriding owned model/rules/type/control events; Maple internal range datePickerProps uses a calendar allowlist. popupProps retains a broad dictionary, with public DatePopupOptions/DateRangePopupOptions recommended and owner keys still filtered at runtime. Cedar timePickerProps configures embedded time presentation; Maple pickerProps configures wheels.

A range placeholder string applies to both endpoints; arrays configure each and missing entries are empty. readonly is separate from disabled; unset field state inherits Form. Cedar range-panel exchangeTime only handles reversed interactive candidates: true swaps their times, false retains endpoint times. It does not reorder external model/text/shortcut values. Maple does not expose this property.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Values and events

`DateValue = Date | string | number`. Invalid dates and incomplete/reversed ranges cannot commit. min/max are inclusive; strings follow value-format, while Date/timestamps are also accepted. Confirmation revalidates rules. `disabledTime` returns numeric lists from `disabledHours()`, `disabledMinutes(hour)`, `disabledSeconds(hour, minute)`. Valid pure panels emit `confirm(value, date(s), text(s))`; fields use `update:open`/`open-change`, not close. Nested panel/popup props configure presentation only, not top-level models/rules/state events. Range disabled accepts [startDisabled, endDisabled]; locked endpoints cannot be cleared/modified.

### Date Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `before-commit` | Explicit field-save guard using payload, done and context | `BeforeFieldCommit` | `undefined` |
| `blur-color` | Color while unfocused | `string` | Theme default |
| `clearable` | Allow clearing with disabled, readonly and pending guards | `boolean` | `true` |
| `date-fields` | Date wheel columns and order; an explicit list controls visibility | `readonly DatePickerField[]`<br>`DatePickerField: 'month' \| 'year' \| 'day'` | Derived from precision |
| `date-picker-props` | Date-panel presentation options, with model/rules/type owned by the field | `DatePickerOptions` | `{}` |
| `default-open` | Initial uncontrolled opening, read only at creation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value, read only at creation | `DateValue \| DateValue[]` | `undefined` |
| `disable-confirm` | Commit on selection; false retains draft for confirmation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | Disable interaction; fields inherit FormItem/Form when unset | `boolean` | Inherited, finally false |
| `disabled-date` | Return true to disable the date; side is start/end | `(date: Date, side: DateSide) => boolean`<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | `undefined` |
| `disabled-time` | Return disabled hour/minute/second lists for a date and endpoint | `(date: Date, side: DateSide) => DateDisabledTime`<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | `undefined` |
| `edit-mode` | Field editing mode, inherited from FormItem/Form when unset | `FieldEditMode`<br>`'direct' \| 'popup'` | Inherited, finally popup |
| `empty-text` | Empty text in read-pretty mode | `string` | Inherited, finally '-' |
| `empty-value` | Clear output or synchronous factory, independent of emptyValues recognition | `DateValue \| null \| (() => DateValue \| null \| undefined)` | `undefined` |
| `empty-values` | Empty-value recognition list, replaced rather than merged | `readonly unknown[]` | Inherited/family default |
| `error` | Field error presentation, inherited when unset | `boolean` | Inherited, finally false |
| `focus-color` | Color while focused | `string` | Theme default |
| `format` | Display/text-input format; a function only formats without reverse text parsing | `string \| ((date: Date) => string)` | From precision/time settings |
| `hint` | Floating placeholder hint, suppressed by an outer Form label | `boolean` | `true` |
| `input-editable` | Allow text input without removing panel selection | `boolean` | `true` |
| `interactive-mode` | Maple calendar viewport mode, independent of field editing mode | `page \| scroll \| line` | `page` |
| `line` | Show the field border or underline | `boolean` | `true` |
| `loading` | Manual loading feedback, independent of event return values | `boolean` | `false` |
| `loading-mode` | Field loading presentation mode | `default \| line` | default |
| `max` | Inclusive maximum; a supplied invalid boundary is not silently ignored | `DateValue` | `undefined` |
| `min` | Inclusive minimum; a supplied invalid boundary is not silently ignored | `DateValue` | `undefined` |
| `model-value` | External date value; undefined is uncontrolled, null is explicitly empty | `DateValue \| DateValue[] \| null` | `undefined` |
| `multiple` | Maple multiple selection; avoid enabling range mode at the same time | `boolean` | `false` |
| `open` | Controlled field editor opening | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `open-trigger-target` | Open by field or icon click, without restricting keyboard opening | `field \| icon` | field |
| `panel-type` | Maple field panel presentation, independent of editMode | `calendar \| picker \| calendarPicker` | `calendar` |
| `picker-props` | Maple date/time wheel presentation options, excluding the root model/rules | `DateWheelOptions` | `{}` |
| `placeholder` | Field placeholder, following Locale when omitted | `string` | `undefined` |
| `popup-container` | Editor container; false renders in place | `PopupContainer` | Shared container default |
| `popup-props` | Trigger presentation options, filtering owned state/model/rules/control listeners at runtime | `Record<string, unknown>` | `{}` |

### DatePicker Events

### DatePicker Slots

`weekIndex` is the nth day of the week, starting at `0` on the weekend

| Name | Description | Prop |
| ---------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `year` | Custom the year in the title | `year: YYYY` |
| `month` | Custom the month in the title | `year: YYYY` <br> `month: MM` |
| `date` | Custom the date in the title | `year: YYYY` <br> `month: MM` <br> `date: DD` <br> `week: weekIndex` |
| `range` | Custom range in the title | `choose: [startData, endDate]` |
| `multiple` | Custom multiple selection in the title | `choose: ['YYYY-MM-DD' \| 'YYYY-MM']` |
| `actions` | Custom the views in the action panel | `{ confirm, disabled }` |

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

## Visible wheel fields

`date-fields` and `time-fields` independently control date and time columns and their order. The two groups do not interleave. Fields and standalone panels share the same props; range endpoints share the configuration.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `date-fields` | readonly DatePickerField[]<br>`DatePickerField: 'month' \| 'year' \| 'day'` | Generate year/month/day columns from type | year, month, day. Only date wheels are affected; the calendar grid is unchanged. |
| `time-fields` | readonly TimePickerField[]<br>`TimePickerField: 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | Hour/minute/second | Controls time wheels, including those embedded in calendars. |

Arrays must be nonempty and unique; explicit arrays strictly determine column visibility/order. Omission uses defaults. Date/time field groups validate separately and cannot mix. Hidden units retain existing values and merge back into the complete draft. Changing field configuration does not commit the model. Nested display options cannot override root props.

Date/DateRange time areas apply only with show-time. `format` controls input text; `value-format` controls saved representation; neither determines panel columns. Unspecified datetime formats save seconds by default. For minute strings, configure both formats explicitly. Hiding year still uses the complete draft year. MM-DD alone cannot represent cross-year ranges; save complete dates for leap-year/cross-year workflows.

Field value/viewport notifications use the corresponding public Emits tuples; DateChangeArgs contains value, date(s) and text(s). Listener Promises are not awaited and do not drive loading. beforeCommit uses payload/done/context, with value/previousValue in payload and signal/optional event in context; undefined waits for done.

### Panel event parameter types

Standalone panels have the seven events below, without the old preview event. Navigation uses picker-value-change and update:pickerValue. Navigation/shortcut hover-focus preview does not imply selection or commit. Confirmation only notifies when valid; select draft is separate from committed change.

| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `DatePickerEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `DatePickerEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `DatePickerEmits['select']` |
| `confirm` | `DatePickerEmits['confirm']` |
| `update:pickerValue` | `DatePickerEmits['update:pickerValue']` |
| `picker-value-change` | `DatePickerEmits['picker-value-change']` |
| `select-shortcut` | `DatePickerEmits['select-shortcut']` |

# Defaults Customization

### Intro

The component library provides the ability to customize the default values of component props.

### Basic Usage

Customize the component's property definition through the mp-static method `setPropsDefaults` provided by the component. It should be noted that attribute customization only takes effect for declarative components, and the customized behavior should be before the component is initialized.

```js
// playground-ignore
// main.ts
import { Button } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

Button.setPropsDefaults({
  status: 'primary',
  variant: 'tonal',
  elevation: 10
})
```

After customization, the following two writing methods will be equivalent.

```html
<!-- playground-ignore -->
<!-- App.vue -->
<template>
  <mp-button>Hello</mp-button>
</template>
```

```html
<!-- playground-ignore -->
<!-- App.vue -->
<template>
  <mp-button status="primary" variant="tonal" :elevation="10">Hello</mp-button>
</template>
```

# Maple Component CSS Variable Reference

Generated from compiled component token declarations. Do not edit tables by hand: run `node bin/token-catalog.mjs --patch` in design-ui and apply the patch; `--check` detects drift.

Use this alongside Design Tokens and CSS Variable Layers: this reference lists exact names, declaration values and consumption evidence, not a claim that all components passed visual acceptance. Values are declarations, not computed pixels; multiple values retain their selector conditions. Runtime theme objects and inline props can override them. Foundation/system roles are explained in the design guide, not duplicated as component APIs here.

Public variables may be overridden on the rendered component root or the real popup ancestor. Internal variables are implementation details and must not be used by applications. Size/variant/status/loading/disabled govern when a token is used; declaration does not imply every state consumes it. CSS property lists describe transitive compiled reachability, not selector visibility or precedence.

## ripple

Source: `src/ripple/style/token.less`

expand-duration / fade-duration reach transform / opacity transitions; runtime also reads their resolved duration/delay from the actual wave to avoid premature fading/removal. The two 250ms minimum lifecycle policies are not CSS tokens. See the design guide for sampling boundaries and cleanup ownership. This indirect timing consumption is not a literal var() runtime reference.

### Countdown business clock and deactivation

### Runtime scheduling is not automatically a motion token

The scanner reports line-level hints, not defects or accepted cases. Classify responsibility first: declarations do not execute; measurement RAF batches geometry reads/writes; interaction delays decide when state is requested; business deadlines control display or polling; visual completion waits follow actual CSS completion. A timeout or RAF alone does not justify replacing the first four responsibilities with CSS duration. Reduced motion must not disable necessary measurement or shorten business deadlines.

The first manually reviewed slice covers 14 files / 18 hints: 6 declarations, 6 measurement schedules, 4 interaction delays and 2 native scrolling calls. Layout forwards caller scrollTo options; smooth scrolling and preference behavior are not certified. Source hashes and quoted lines guard review drift; changes require re-review, not automatic hash refresh. The other 159 hints are not yet in this classification ledger, including previously audited components; they are not 159 unfixed defects. This classification adds zero browser/OS passes and changes no token layers, defaults or public API.

Current step 6 validation: 80 foreground/solid-fill role checks and 64 primary-white-foreground checks pass. Of 200 foreground/neutral-surface contrast pairs, 94 fall below 4.5:1; this palette does not claim universal ordinary-text contrast compliance.

The current palette uses step 6. Earlier step 7 contrast figures are historical and do not describe the current palette. Solid primary buttons retain white text.

Local reduce rules work with isolated component styles: Cedar disables root/enter/leave transitions and decorative icon fades; Maple disables transitions and animated displacement while preserving standalone horizontal/center translation. Message duration is a business display deadline, not a CSS transition token. Restart, hover pause, clear, deactivation and unmount invalidate stale callbacks; execution checks activity and open. ### Button contrast and palette step 6

Overrides are not automatically corrected or prohibited, but default acceptance does not certify arbitrary business colors. Record an intentional lower-contrast exception rather than claiming AA compliance.

> This page mirrors the shared standard. `design-ui/standards/design-tokens.md` is the source of truth; update this page and the Cedar page whenever the standard changes.

Cedar and Maple share logical token semantics. Only the platform prefix differs: `--c-` for Cedar and `--mp-` for Maple. Shared semantics do not require every platform dimension to be identical, but tokens with the same logical name must have the same responsibility.

## Preserve token responsibilities during refactoring (2026-10-09)

After sharing component structure or changing the DOM, verify the complete path from each public token to its terminal CSS property again. Keeping a declaration and documentation does not prove customization still works. Internal adapters connect platform defaults; they must not merge distinct motion responsibilities or bypass existing public controls with constants.

For Rate, `--{p}-rate-transition-duration` controls ordinary color/hover transitions, `--{p}-rate-scale-duration` controls the selection scale animation, and `--{p}-rate-transition-timing-function` controls both easing curves (p is c or mp). Platform defaults may differ, but all three controls must have real consumers. Declare internal mappings on the component root rather than :root so public overrides on an instance or its ancestors resolve in the correct scope. Reduced-motion preferences disable these effects.

Documentation layout is not a component token API. Site styles own breakpoints, navigation and preview placement; these do not belong in system color or component geometry contracts. Long variable tables scroll locally. Record consumer checks, responsive layout, keyboard navigation and real-device acceptance separately.

### Optional overrides and instance-size fallbacks

VerificationCode's public `--{p}-verification-code-cell-height`, `cell-max-width` and `input-font-size` tokens default to `initial`: this means no explicit override, not a final pixel value. For these unregistered custom properties, `initial` activates the consuming `var()` fallback, which reads the private mapping for the current instance size. Do not resolve component-local private dimensions at `:root`.

`cell-height` controls cell height; `cell-max-width` is the preferred cell width and may shrink when space is limited; `input-font-size` controls character size; `gutter` controls the gap. The first three follow the xs/sm/md/lg/xl field dimensions unless overridden. Gutter defaults to system space-2; the gutter prop writes an inline value to that public token. Override public tokens on an instance or business container, without depending on private mappings or assuming identical desktop/mobile pixel values.

This is an explicit optional-override → instance-size contract, not a fallback for a missing system token. Set a token to `initial` on an instance to restore its size mapping. `unset` inherits ordinary custom properties from ancestors and is not an equivalent reset. Verify mixed sizes, a customized instance and an untouched neighbor across themes and narrow layouts.

## Rules for the consolidated token model

Shared names mean shared responsibilities, not identical desktop and touch density. Every system default is now registered: common values in `systemTokenValues`, explicit control-height/layer differences in `platformSystemTokenValues`. Component defaults follow the same division between `componentTokenValues` and `platformComponentTokenValues`. A token cannot have both a shared default and a platform exception.

Use system spacing, typography, ordinary radius and state-transition roles where their meaning matches. Do not bind an icon, badge dot or layout compensation to control-height merely because the pixels happen to match. Component-specific shape, ratios, structural values and looping animation durations can remain component parameters with an explicit reason. Reduced-motion must suppress unnecessary transitions and loops.

Disabled/readonly are behavior constraints that child closable/checkable props cannot bypass. Pressed, persistently selected and focused are distinct states; each component specifies their overlap with hover. FieldDecorator owns the filled shell; Form must not repaint it. Custom colors and Teleport roots require checking the actual rendered ancestor and composited background, not just the trigger element.

### Message emphasis levels

| Variant | Responsibility | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| neutral | Overlay surface, primary content, semantic status icon, secondary close control. | Cedar |
| tonal | Low-emphasis status surface with readable content and semantic icon. | Explicit on both |
| solid | High-emphasis status fill with paired foreground; default/loading use a dedicated dark surface. | Maple |

Both platforms expose `message-{variant}-{status}-{bg|content-color|icon-color|border-color|close-color}`. Status is default/info/success/warning/danger/loading. Existing defaults and geometry remain intact; Maple's previous solid appearance is not called tonal. Migrate old implicit colors directly to the explicit variant without aliases. A shared border-color role does not require adding a mobile border width.

### Definition, consumption and verification

A variable needs an actual CSS, cross-component, reviewed runtime or finite dynamic consumer. Documentation, comments, theme assignment and circular aliases alone are not evidence. Remove ineffective legacy entries; connect declared customization when a real DOM role exists. Generated tables describe transitive CSS reachability, not visual acceptance. Update source, contracts, state/override tests, reference docs and migration notes together. `check:token-reference` prevents generated documentation drift.

## Four layers

| Layer | Responsibility | External use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foundation / reference | Raw palettes and scales | Applications should not depend on it directly |
| System | Stable semantics shared by components | Global themes may override it |
| Component | Public customization for one component | Preferred application-level entry point |
| Internal | Component implementation details | External use is forbidden |

## System color semantics

System colors cover surfaces (`page / default / raised / overlay / muted / tooltip`), content (`primary / secondary / tertiary / decorative / disabled / on-dark / on-bright / brand / info / success / warning / danger`), borders (`subtle / default / strong`), primary actions, semantic statuses, and shared interaction states. `on-dark` and `on-bright` are paired foregrounds for known dark and bright surfaces; `decorative` applies only to non-text decoration. Cedar and Maple must map each system color role to the same logical foundation value. `theme-contract.json#systemTokenValues` governs these mappings. Governed public component defaults are registered in `componentTokenValues`; FieldDecorator, Collapse, Dialog, Card, Divider, Empty, and Avatar color semantics are currently covered. Dialog borders, sizing, and layout may differ by platform. Card's floating-button container uses `content-primary` on the expanded card surface; its fixed dark close button uses `content-on-dark`. The `#212121` button background is Card-specific, not the global primary action. Divider lines use `border-default` and labels use `content-secondary`; text spacing is `16px` on Cedar and `8px` on Maple. Empty descriptions use `content-tertiary`, while decorative icons use `content-decorative`. Matching hard-coded values across platforms are not sufficient: component defaults and theme overrides should use the correct system semantics.

Pre-release Card token migration: `--mp-card-close-button-primary-color` → `--mp-card-close-button-background`, without a compatibility alias.

Avatar's governed roles are `content-primary` for text, count, and button icon; `surface-default` for borders; and `content-on-dark` only for the icon over the dark scrim. The default `fill-4` background, `fill-2 → fill-3` trigger-button hover step, and translucent scrim remain component visual values. When changing an instance background with `color`, check text contrast and override `--mp-avatar-text-color` if needed: a system role does not guarantee contrast against an arbitrary background. Maple's dark Avatar background `#303030` is theme-specific.

Badge phase three: fills use `status-*` / `action-primary`, while outline text and borders use `content-info/success/warning/danger/brand`. Neutral default outlines use `content-primary`; secondary and tertiary outlines use `content-secondary`. The public outline background works for all statuses, including instances using `color`. Both libraries use light text for the filled primary Badge in the Maple light brand. Compiled CSS checks cover 640 built-in color combinations and 64 outline-background overrides: minimum text contrast is 4.56:1 for fills and 4.97:1 for outlines. Recheck custom colors and backgrounds; unregistered variables remain pending.

The brand content role uses primary palette step 6; the other semantic content roles also use palette step 6 for readable colored text, icons, and matching borders on ordinary neutral surfaces. `content-brand` differs from the main content hierarchy (`content-primary`) and primary action emphasis (`action-primary`); changing the action color alone does not change brand text.

## Public and internal component tokens

Public component tokens use `--mp-{component}-...`, must be documented, and should reference system tokens by default. Applications should customize this layer first.

CSS variables written per instance by props (such as `--mp-divider-opacity`) are runtime value channels, not necessarily theme tokens with `:root` defaults. Component docs must identify their source.

Internal tokens use `--mp-internal-{component}-...`. They support private layout, measurement, or unstable implementation details and must not be used by themes, applications, or public documentation. Promote an internal token to a documented component token when external customization is required.

## Selection order

1. Reuse an existing public component token.
2. Use or introduce a system token for cross-component semantics.
3. Add a public component token for externally customizable component-specific behavior.
4. Use an internal token only for implementation details.
5. Never add unused compatibility aliases to create superficial parity.

Platform control density, touch targets, safe areas, hover capability, and layer implementation may differ. System color roles, same-name component token responsibilities, state names, and public/private boundaries may not differ.

## Complete system-token catalog

Use `--{p}-` below for the platform prefix: `p=c` in Cedar and `p=mp` in Maple. `theme-contract.json#tokens.system` is the machine-checkable list; `systemTokenValues` governs the shared color mappings. Themes may alter palette values, but must not redefine a role's responsibility.

| Color role | Foundation mapping | Intended use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `surface-page` | `color-bg-1` | Application page background, not dialogs. |
| `surface-default` | `color-bg-2` | Ordinary containers and cards. |
| `surface-raised` | `color-bg-3` | Raised content such as Dialog. |
| `surface-overlay` | `color-bg-5` | Higher popup content surfaces, not translucent scrims. |
| `surface-tooltip` | `#373739` | Dark hint surface in both modes; pair with on-dark. |
| `scrim` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` | Translucent backdrop, not a content surface. |
| `surface-muted` | `color-fill-1` | Weak filled surfaces and default filled controls. |
| `content-primary` | `color-text-1` | Main text, headings, and icons on ordinary surfaces. |
| `content-secondary` | `color-text-2` | Supporting text, secondary actions, and Divider labels. |
| `content-brand` | `primary-6` (RGB) | Brand text, icons, and matching borders on ordinary neutral surfaces. |
| `content-info` | `blue-6` (RGB) | Info text, icons, and matching borders on ordinary neutral surfaces. |
| `content-success` | `success-6` (RGB) | Success text, icons, and matching borders on ordinary neutral surfaces. |
| `content-warning` | `warning-6` (RGB) | Warning text, icons, and matching borders on ordinary neutral surfaces. |
| `content-danger` | `danger-6` (RGB) | Danger text, icons, and matching borders on ordinary neutral surfaces. |
| `content-tertiary` | `color-text-3` | Placeholders and low-emphasis descriptions; verify contrast. |
| `content-decorative` | `color-text-4` | Non-text decoration, such as Empty icons; not readable text. |
| `content-disabled` | `color-text-disabled` | Truly disabled content, not decoration. |
| `content-on-dark` | `color-white` | Text and icons on a known dark surface only. |
| `content-on-bright` | `color-black` | Text and icons on a known bright surface; remains dark in dark mode and requires per-pair contrast checks. |
| `border-subtle/default/strong` | `color-border-1/2/4` | Weak separators, ordinary outlines, stronger interaction outlines. |
| `action-primary` | `color-primary` | Brand actions and focus emphasis, not any dark surface. |
| `status-info/success/warning/danger` | Matching `color-*` palette roles | Status fills and emphasis; readable text on ordinary surfaces uses the matching `content-*` role. |
| `state-hover` | `color-fill-2` | Neutral hover surface on hover-capable devices. |
| `state-selected` | `color-primary-light-1` | Brand-tinted selection surface, not a pressed state. |

| Other system category | Tokens and values | Design purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spacing | `space-1…8`: `2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 20 / 24px` | Shared padding and gap rhythm. |
| Radius | `radius-sm/md/lg/pill`: `2 / 4 / 8 / 999px` | Control, container, and pill shapes; a circular avatar's `50%` is component geometry. |
| Type size | `font-size-xs/sm/md/lg/xl`: `12 / 13 / 14 / 16 / 18px` | Reusable component text scale. |
| Type weight | `font-weight-regular/medium/semibold`: `400 / 500 / 600` | Normal and emphasized text. |
| Motion | `motion-duration-fast/standard/slow`: `120 / 180 / 240ms`; `motion-easing-standard`: `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` | Common transitions; respect reduced-motion preferences. |
| Layer | `layer-behind/base/raised`: `-1 / 0 / 1`; `layer-popup/modal`: platform mappings | Relative stack roles, not identical absolute z-indexes. |
| Controls | `control-height-xs/sm/md/lg/xl`, `control-touch-target` | Cedar heights: `28/32/36/40/44px`; Maple: `44/48/52/56/60px`. Both use a `44px` touch target. |

## Designing component tokens

A public name should identify the component, optional part, visual branch, interaction state, and the CSS property it controls: `--{p}-{component}-{part?}-{variant/status/size?}-{state?}-{property}`. Omit dimensions that do not change. Use `background` for a background and `text-color` for text; do not call a dark neutral background `primary-color`. Component defaults normally reference system roles. Component-specific geometry or contrast surfaces may use a documented local value when no cross-component semantic role exists.

Create a state token only when its value differs. State precedence must be explicit in selectors, not accidental source order: a filled input uses `fill-1` by default, `fill-2` on hover, and `fill-3` on focus; focus wins if hover and focus coexist. `focus-visible` means keyboard-visible focus, not every focus event. Disabled controls must not retain hover or focus emphasis.

The preferred resolution path is `foundation → system → component → CSS consumer`. Override a public component token for one component, or a system token/palette value for a global theme. Theme files that override component tokens must preserve their semantics. If a custom background changes, review text, icon, border, and state contrast together. Do not use a `var()` fallback to hide a missing internal system token.

Per-instance variables written from props, such as Divider's `--mp-divider-opacity`, are runtime value channels and may have no `:root` default. Private `--mp-internal-{component}-...` variables are implementation details and must not be promised to consumers. Document whether each CSS variable is a static default, a theme override, or a runtime value.

## Cross-platform change checklist

1. Identify the visual role before choosing a value. Matching hard-coded values do not prove semantic consistency.
2. Reuse an exact existing role; if none fits, define a new system role or document a component exception. Never force an approximate role merely to pass checks.
3. Align Cedar and Maple names, consuming CSS properties, defaults, and theme overrides. Record justified density, touch, or layout differences.
4. Register shared values in `componentTokenValues`; register new system names in `tokens.system` and mappings in `systemTokenValues`. Update component docs and both menu mirrors.
5. Verify light/dark themes, combined hover/focus/disabled states, resolvable references, relevant tests, contract checks, docs, and diff formatting.

FieldDecorator, Collapse, Dialog, Card, Divider, Empty, and Avatar have governed key color defaults; Badge is partially governed. Other existing variables are not automatically compliant. Public renames require a migration mapping and release-stage review; do not keep unused aliases silently.

## Tag: semantic colors and selection

Tag default uses a soft surface, unlike Badge's strong filled background. Semantic text and outline borders use content-brand/info/success/warning/danger; secondary and tertiary use content-secondary. Colored status backgrounds use palette step 1 (primary/blue/success/warning/danger), secondary uses gray-2 and tertiary gray-1. These are component-specific paired surfaces, not new system roles. Neutral default text/icon use content-primary/content-secondary; custom filled text defaults to content-on-dark and requires a sufficiently dark background.

Unchecked checkable tags stay neutral, including hover. Checked semantic colors win over generic hover. Checked neutral default uses fill-2 → fill-3, while checked outline stays transparent. Loading suppresses the governed neutral/status hover feedback. Non-checkable tags render as checked. The controlled checked event contract is unchanged.

color takes precedence over status. text-color explicitly customizes text. Preset palette colors are not semantic status roles. Preset outline/hover/dark token behavior is now governed below; custom contrast, geometry and motion remain outside this batch; Tag is only partially governed. Desktop/mobile dimensions remain intentionally different. Component documentation lists every token and its current default.

The shared contract adds 28 Tag defaults. Run pnpm check:tag-themes in design-ui: compiled Less is checked across both libraries, both brands and both modes, 8 statuses, 2 variants, checked/hover/loading combinations (1024 cascade cases). 640 selected, non-hover, non-loading foreground/background pairs across five system surfaces meet 4.5:1 (minimum 4.681:1). The script uses DOM selector matching and a specificity evaluator for the current selectors; it is not browser visual QA. Preset/custom colors, arbitrary backgrounds and loading opacity are excluded. Extend the checker when selector structures change.

## Alert: information semantics and theme inheritance

Alert has info/success/warning/danger/default statuses and standard/tonal/outline variants. Colored titles, content, icons and outline borders use the corresponding system content roles, not status fill colors. Neutral titles use content-primary, content/icons use content-secondary and borders use border-default.

Standard uses palette step 1 surfaces and step 3 decorative borders; tonal uses the same surface without a border. Outline stays transparent with readable content-colored borders. Neutral filled backgrounds remain component-specific fill-2 surfaces, not a hover role. Title/content/icon tokens remain independent public customization points. The content token also supplies root inheritance for the close icon and unstyled action/slot content; explicitly styled children retain their own colors.

Maple dark inherits the shared color defaults through its dark palette instead of replacing them with separate translucent fills or another info palette. Existing mobile dark geometry is preserved and remains outside color governance. The color prop changes only the background; callers must verify all foregrounds when customizing it. Weak standard borders are decorative and are not guaranteed to meet interactive-control boundary contrast requirements.

All 65 Alert color defaults are registered; geometry/motion remain pending. Run pnpm check:alert-themes (or node bin/alert-theme-check.mjs) in design-ui. Compiled Less covers 120 platform/brand/mode/variant/status combinations, 3000 foreground pairs across five system surfaces, minimum 4.802:1, plus local title/content/icon overrides. Custom backgrounds and independently styled slots are excluded. Selector/cascade checks do not replace browser visual QA. Tag and Alert share the audit utilities.

## Button milestone: variants and interaction colors

This milestone covers Button color/state semantics, not every component or all geometry/motion. All eight statuses, four variants, icon-container, both brands/modes and hover/active/focus-visible/disabled/loading are included without changing Props or events.

The historical status-color tokens now mean solid default backgrounds only. status-text-color controls their contrasting foreground: on-bright for colored/secondary fills, on-dark for light tertiary (on-bright in dark mode), content-primary for neutral default. Maple light's deep orange primary uses on-dark. Historical status-icon-color means readable content for text/outline/tonal and default icon-container, using content-brand/status roles and neutral content roles. status-icon-container-color supplies their soft surfaces: palette step 1, gray-2/1 for secondary/tertiary, surface-muted for default. These historical names remain documented rather than duplicated with aliases. Maple dark inherits the same semantics and only retains geometry overrides.

Solid/tonal/icon-container state opacity is 0.08 hover and 0.12 active. Text/outline use their soft container at 0.5 hover and 1 active, controlled by plain-state-opacity-hover/active. Solid status-state-layer-color is paired with its foreground; neutral default uses content-primary. The shared state-layer-color (surface-page) applies to tonal/icon-container, not every variant. internal-button-state-* variables are private branch-resolution channels. Layers paint behind content inside an isolated stacking context. Active wins hover; blocked states suppress both. Focus-visible is an independent content-brand ring (2px width/offset), not the solid foreground color.

Disabled tokens outrank variant/status/icon-container and suspend color/text-color inline overrides until re-enabled. Loading preserves the palette but blocks interaction; indicators default to currentColor unless loading-color is supplied. Custom colors/styles/slots require the caller to verify contrast. Transient ripple and disabled contrast are excluded from the enabled-text contrast guarantee.

The Button phase added 13 public state-layer tokens and 48 defaults, bringing the total at that milestone to 223; see the floating phase for the current total. Run pnpm check:button-themes or node bin/button-theme-check.mjs in design-ui. Compiled CSS checks 12288 cascade cases and 40960 foreground/background pairs across five surfaces (minimum 4.563:1), plus component interaction tests. Browser spot checks cover basic light/dark variants, disabled styles, keyboard focus and hover stacking. This is not exhaustive cross-browser visual testing; global lint/snapshot debt remains separate. Complete root defaults and theme exceptions are listed in component documentation.

## Floating surfaces, scrims, and arrows

This phase covers Tooltip, Popover, Overlay and Trigger. Two shared roles are added: `sys-color-surface-tooltip: #373739` is a consistently dark compact hint surface in both modes, paired with `content-on-dark` (not a mode-inverting surface); `sys-color-scrim: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` dims obscured content without fading foreground children. `surface-overlay` remains the solid popup content surface mapped to `color-bg-5`, never a scrim.

Colored Tooltip statuses use action/status fills with `content-on-bright`. Both libraries use `content-on-dark` for the deep-orange Maple light primary. Maple dark no longer overrides Tooltip colors/opacity, Popover background or Overlay background. Default Tooltip opacity is 1 in every built-in theme. Custom opacity/colors require fresh contrast checks.

Tooltip and Popover arrows share their component background with the panel; Popover also shares its border. Wrapper arrow selectors outrank Trigger defaults even if Trigger CSS loads last. Standalone Trigger only defines an arrow, not a business content surface.

Customize public component variables on the actual popup scope (for example via `popup-style`); variables on a reference button do not automatically inherit across Teleport. Tooltip `color` sets panel and arrow backgrounds, while `text-color` sets content text. Explicit `content-style` and `arrow-style` win on their respective nodes; changing one does not synchronize the other. Use `--mp-popover-background` on the popup scope to customize both Popover parts. Internal geometry variables are not public styling APIs. Overlay colors only the backdrop.

The contract adds 35 defaults (Tooltip 23, Popover 4 colors, Overlay 3, Trigger 5), totaling 64 system names, 29 governed system values, and 258 component values. Platform exceptions remain: Popover shadows differ; Maple dark Tooltip keeps 4px radius, 14px font, 8px/16px vertical/horizontal padding; Maple dark Popover keeps a 2px radius. These density exceptions are not semantic differences. Dialog/Popup were outside this floating phase; see the subsequent modal surface phase below.

`check:floating-themes` joins the shared checks: 72 compiled-CSS theme combinations, 320 text pairs across five host surfaces, minimum contrast 5.178:1, plus arrow/panel agreement, public override consumption, and Trigger-last order regression. This is not browser layout testing and excludes arbitrary custom colors, opacity and animation intermediate frames.

## Modal surface phase: Dialog, Drawer and Popup

Both Dialog implementations, Cedar Drawer and Maple Popup now use `sys-color-scrim` through their public backdrop tokens. All three content surfaces use `surface-raised`. Drawer and Popup remain platform-specific components; no unused aliases are created on the other platform.

Maple Dialog previously declared an unconsumed backdrop token referencing a missing foundation variable while rendering a Popup-styled backdrop. Its scoped selector now consumes `dialog-overlay-background`, survives Popup-last loading and leaves standalone Popup unchanged. Maple dark no longer overrides Dialog background/title/content colors or Popup surface/scrim. Dialog status icons use readable `content-info/success/warning/danger` roles rather than status fills.

Drawer uses `content-primary` for header/body (including the close button), `border-default` for separators, and retains geometry. Its unused close-icon-right variable was removed without an alias; header layout and close-btn-margin-left control the close button. Its Less no longer embeds the entire theme; the style entry still imports the foundation.

Popup adds `--mp-popup-content-text-color` mapped to `content-primary`, paired with its raised background. Both defaults are disabled by `unstyled`. Declarations now live in token.less.

### Customization and inheritance

Use system scrim for a global theme and component backdrop tokens for local changes. Apply backdrop variables with overlay-style; Dialog/Drawer panel styles and Popup content style do not inherit to sibling backdrops. Teleport follows actual DOM ancestry, not the Vue call site. Explicit backgroundColor overrides token consumption. Use color alpha, not parent opacity, to dim a backdrop. Multiple scrims still compose and darken; this phase does not change modal stacking behavior.

### Contract and verification

Five existing Dialog mappings changed (scrim plus four status icons). Shared totals stay at 64 system names, 29 governed system values and 258 component values. Five Cedar Drawer colors and three Maple Popup colors are checked by `check:modal-themes` separately from shared defaults.

Compiled Less checks cover 16 platform/brand/mode combinations and 72 foreground pairs, minimum 5.102:1, plus public/global overrides, Dialog/Popup isolation, unstyled behavior and load order. Component regression tests inspect real Teleport targets without transition stubs. This is not browser visual/animation validation; arbitrary custom colors, stacked scrims and intermediate animation frames are excluded. Platform geometry, radius, shadow, timing and layer defaults remain unchanged. Other dark translucent surfaces still need purpose-specific review.

## Feedback phase: Message, Notification and LoadingBar (historical)

> This records the pre-variant milestone. Its old Message names and pending migration have been superseded by the three-variant model above.

This phase governs both Message implementations, Cedar Notification and Maple LoadingBar. Semantics are aligned without silently replacing mobile colored toasts with desktop neutral panels.

Cedar Message/Notification use surface-overlay, border-default, primary content and secondary close controls. Status icons use readable content roles; info is no longer a primary brand fill, loading uses content-brand, and Notification's existing error maps to content-danger. The neutral Notification icon token now has an actual consumer. Panel roots provide readable inherited text for plain action/footer content.

Maple Message keeps its component-specific #333 neutral/loading surface paired with content-on-dark. Colored backgrounds use status fills with content-on-bright. Four public tokens are added: `--mp-message-{info|success|warning|danger}-color`. The general message-color only controls neutral/loading. Icons, plain action content, close controls and currentColor focus outlines inherit the status foreground. Styled slots and child controls must ensure their own contrast.

LoadingBar uses content-brand/content-danger for normal/error strokes: a thin indicator must be distinguishable from its host surface. color/errorColor options override defaults. Custom colors and backdrops require fresh checks.

Cedar Message/Notification rely on the style entry for foundation imports instead of embedding the theme in component Less. Geometry, shadow, motion, remaining legacy consumers and close-control interaction details are outside this phase. ## Input and menu color phase: Input, AutoComplete and Select

This phase adds 26 shared color defaults: 5 Input, 10 AutoComplete and 11 Select. The total becomes 284; system names/values remain 64/29 and shared component-name contracts remain 35. No public variables were added or renamed.

Input counter-color keeps its field-suffix-text-color dependency. The four input-feedback-{success|warning|error|validating}-color variables now use content-{success|warning|danger|brand}. They color feedback SVGs, not the input background, caret or focus ring. Overriding field-error-color/field-focus-color no longer recolors feedback icons; use the corresponding input-feedback token. FieldDecorator still owns the filled fill1 → fill2 → fill3 progression.

Maple's historical dark Field overrides changed filled states back to fill2/fill3/plain background and replaced content, auxiliary, error and border colors. These color overrides are removed while geometry remains. The audit explicitly loads dark/field.ts so theme overrides cannot silently bypass the existing FieldDecorator semantic contract.

For AutoComplete and Select, popup-bg uses surface-overlay and popup-border-color uses border-default. Default/selected/disabled option backgrounds use surface-overlay; hover uses state-hover. Default/hover/selected text uses content-primary; disabled text uses content-disabled. AutoComplete retains option-bg-default and option-text-color-default naming, while Select uses popup-option-bg and popup-option-text-color. Remaining option suffixes map directly with Select's popup- prefix. Select's popup-group-title-text-color uses content-secondary: a small section heading is readable content, not a disabled label.

AutoComplete maps its public variables onto Select variables locally on its dropdown. Customize the owning component's tokens rather than relying on that adapter. Maple dark no longer supplies separate selected colors. Both platforms derive the same roles from their system theme.

Menu active means keyboard navigation, not pressed state. Color priority is disabled > active/hover > selected > default. Selected font weight remains in effect; custom selected colors still yield to hover while navigating.

The shared check:selection-themes command compiles real Less for both platforms, two brands and light/dark modes: 384 states and 296 contrast pairs. Text/counters/group headings require 4.5:1; non-text feedback icons require 3:1. The overall minimum 3.991:1 belongs to an icon check, not a lower text threshold. Disabled states are checked for precedence and consumption without claiming text contrast compliance. Sentinel colors verify actual public-variable consumers, including the local AutoComplete adapter.

This is not browser visual testing and excludes arbitrary slot colors/backgrounds, pseudo-elements, animation frames and Teleport inheritance. Place popup overrides on actual DOM ancestors or the popup root. Geometry, shadows, Input sizing and Select's historical highlight variables remain outside this phase, as do Checkbox/Radio/Switch/Form/Textarea tokens.

## Choice controls: color roles and state priority (historical)
