### Auto Size

Auto sizing converts the measured box to the actual CSS box model, counting padding and the top/bottom borders once. Explicit `minRows / maxRows` override the theme minimum; excess content scrolls within the row cap. Turning auto size off restores native height and the platform resize default. Compare both box models, fill six lines, and switch the cap.

Example source: src/textarea/example/demos/auto-size.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const content = ref('第一行 / First line')
const boundedContent = ref('第一行 / First line\n第二行 / Second line')
const maxRows = ref(5)
function fill() {
  boundedContent.value = 'one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\nfive\nsix'
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="lg" fill>
    <mp-textarea default-value="原生三行 / Native three rows" :rows="3" aria-label="Native rows" />
    <mp-textarea v-model="content" auto-size placeholder="随内容增高 / Grow with content" />
    <mp-space wrap>
      <mp-button @click="fill">填入六行 / Fill six lines</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="maxRows = maxRows === 5 ? 2 : 5">切换行数上限 / Toggle row limit: {{ maxRows }}</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <template v-for="box in ['border-box', 'content-box']" :key="box">
      <p>{{ box }} · 2–{{ maxRows }} rows</p>
      <mp-textarea
        v-model="boundedContent"
        :auto-size="{ minRows: 2, maxRows }"
        :textarea-attrs="{
          'aria-label': 'Bounded ' + box,
          style: {
            boxSizing: box,
            lineHeight: '20px',
            padding: '4px',
            borderStyle: 'solid',
            borderWidth: '1px 2px 3px 4px',
          },
        }"
      />
    </template>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Body and event contract

Input notifies input → update:modelValue. Clearing notifies clear → input → update:modelValue → change once each, with one corresponding Form notification. Clearing is blocked while readonly, disabled or composing. Rejected controlled proposals restore the native content, including input types without cursor APIs.

Example source: src/textarea/example/demos/en-US/body-contract.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('Editable content')
const events = ref<string[]>([])
const record = (name: string) => {
  events.value = [...events.value.slice(-7), name]
}
</script>
<template>
  <div class="textarea-body-demo">
    <mp-textarea
      v-model="value"
      hint
      clearable
      placeholder="Work notes"
      :auto-size="{ minRows: 2, maxRows: 5 }"
      :max-length="100"
      show-word-limit
      @clear="record('clear')"
      @input="record('input')"
      @update:model-value="record('update:modelValue')"
      @change="record('change')"
    />
    <mp-textarea :line="false" hint placeholder="Borderless hint" focus-color="#137547" :rows="2" />
    <p>Enter inserts a newline; blur commits; clearing notifies each semantic once.</p>
    <output>{{ events.join(' → ') || 'Waiting for interaction' }}</output>
  </div>
</template>
<style scoped>
.textarea-body-demo {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 16px;
}
.textarea-body-demo p {
  margin: 0;
}
</style>
```

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Value model and interaction

### Dynamic empty values

Changing empty-value (including its factory) affects the next clear operation. Changing empty-values reformats the existing model without emitting a model update. Direct clear publishes immediately; deferred clear remains a draft until confirmation.

Example source: src/textarea/example/demos/empty-policy.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const sentinel = ref(false)
const emptyValue = computed(() => (sentinel.value ? 'CLEARED' : null))
const emptyValues = [undefined, null, '', 'CLEARED']
const direct = ref('Direct draft')
const deferred = ref('Deferred draft')
function reset() {
  direct.value = 'Direct draft'
  deferred.value = 'Deferred draft'
}
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column">
    <mp-space>
      <mp-button @click="sentinel = !sentinel">切换清空值 / Toggle empty value</mp-button>
      <mp-button @click="reset">重置示例 / Reset values</mp-button>
    </mp-space>
    <p role="status">empty-value: {{ JSON.stringify(emptyValue) }}</p>
    <mp-textarea
      v-model="direct"
      edit-mode="direct"
      :empty-value="emptyValue"
      :empty-values="emptyValues"
      clearable
      aria-label="Direct text"
      placeholder="直接编辑 / Direct"
    />
    <mp-textarea
      v-model="deferred"
      edit-mode="popup"
      :empty-value="emptyValue"
      :empty-values="emptyValues"
      clearable
      aria-label="Deferred text"
      placeholder="确认后保存 / Deferred"
    />
    <p>
      先切换清空值再清空；延迟编辑确认后回写。Change the policy before clearing; deferred changes publish on confirm.
    </p>
    <pre class="empty-policy-model">{{ JSON.stringify({ direct, deferred }) }}</pre>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Composition input

IME composition preserves the native text being entered; external model updates do not replace it before composition completes. Existing formatting and controlled-owner acceptance apply after completion. Queued restoration from an earlier input cannot replace the text or caret of a later edit or composition. Length limits and modifiers retain their existing post-composition input/commit timing.

## Usage notes

### Sizing and native methods

size supports five FieldDecorator densities: xs/sm/md/lg/xl. rows, auto-size and Textarea tokens still control textarea height/text metrics. Cedar allows manual resize by default; Maple does not. InputGroup/Form state is inherited, with explicit child values taking precedence. Exposes focus(options?), blur(), select() and textareaRef.

`TextareaProps`、`TextareaVariant`、`TextareaMaxLength`、`TextareaAutoSize`、`TextareaEmits`、`TextareaSlots`、`TextareaExpose`、`TextareaInstance`。

Native methods: `focus(options?: FocusOptions)`, `blur()`, `select()`; `textareaRef` is the native element.

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / popup`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Maple uses edit-mode="popup" to open the editor when the value area is clicked; direct edits immediately. readPretty is a reading-only setting, independent of readonly and disabled.

FormItem validates the candidate first and keeps editing open on failure; before-commit approval runs after validation succeeds. See the property section above for approval parameters and completion rules.

`open / default-open / update:open / open-change` control and report editor visibility; `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes reading content. See Form for composed examples.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

`--mp-field-caret-color` defaults to `currentColor` and sets shared caret color. `--mp-textarea-caret-color` overrides this component, default `var(--mp-field-caret-color)`.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Textarea Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| empty-value | Clear output; omission clears to an empty string and manual deletion is unchanged | `string \| null \| (() => string \| null)` | `undefined` |
| model-value | Controlled value | `string \| null` | `-` |
| model-modifiers | `v-model` modifiers; supports `trim` | `object` | `{}` |
| default-value | Uncontrolled initial value; read only at creation, never written into the parent | `string` | `''` |
| placeholder | Placeholder or floating hint text | `string` | `-` |
| disabled | Whether disabled | `boolean` | `false` |
| readonly | Whether readonly | `boolean` | `false` |
| variant | `filled`, `outline`, or `standard` | `string` | `outline` |
| size | `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, or `xl` | `ComponentSize`<br>`'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `md` |
| error | Show the error state | `boolean` | `false` |
| max-length | Finite nonnegative length or `{ length, errorOnly? }`; 0 is unlimited; invalid values diagnose and fall back to no limit | `number \| object` | `0` |
| show-word-limit | Show the character counter | `boolean` | `false` |
| clearable | Show a persistent clear icon while editable and nonempty | `boolean` | `false` |
| word-length | Custom length calculator | `function` | `-` |
| word-slice | Custom truncation function | `function` | `-` |
| aria-label | Accessible label | `string` | `-` |
| autofocus | Focus automatically after mount | `boolean` | `false` |
| enterkeyhint | Mobile enter-key hint | `string` | `-` |
| hint | Use the placeholder as a floating hint | `boolean` | `true` |
| line | Show the border or bottom separator | `boolean` | `true` |
| text-color | Text color | `string` | `-` |
| focus-color | Focus color | `string` | `-` |
| blur-color | Blur color | `string` | `-` |
| rows | Positive integer native rows, including numeric strings; invalid values diagnose and restore native default rows. Theme constraints still affect visual height | `string \| number` | Native default `2` |
| resize | Allow vertical resizing; ignored while a valid automatic-height policy is active | `boolean` | `false` |
| auto-size | Automatic height; row budgets must be positive and finite, with minRows no greater than maxRows. Invalid configurations diagnose and disable measurement | `boolean \| { minRows?: number; maxRows?: number }` | `false` |
| textarea-attrs | Additional native textarea attributes; cannot override controlled value, state, rows, length policy, or component events | `Record<string, unknown>` | `undefined` |
| edit-mode | Editor mode; inherits FormItem/Form | `direct / popup` | `undefined` |
| read-pretty | Reading presentation; inherits FormItem/Form | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| empty-values | Empty-value recognition set; an explicit value replaces the inherited set | `readonly unknown[]` | Inherited component-family policy |
| empty-text | Empty reading text; inherits FormItem/Form | `string` | `'-'` |
| before-commit | Deferred save approval: (payload, done, context) | `BeforeFieldCommit` | `undefined` |
| open | Controlled editor visibility in deferred modes | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| default-open | Uncontrolled initial editor visibility; creation-only | `boolean` | `false` |
| popup-container | Deferred editor portal target; false renders in place | `PopupContainer` | `undefined` |
| loading | Manual loading presentation; remains editable | `boolean` | `false` |
| loading-mode | Indicator layout | `default / line` | `default` |

`rows` accepts a positive integer or a numeric string convertible to one. Invalid values use Vue prop-validation diagnostics and restore native default `rows`. `auto-size` minRows/maxRows accept positive finite line-height multiples, including fractions; minRows must not exceed maxRows. Invalid objects disable automatic measurement and clear its previous calculated styles. Null is treated as unset.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` approves saving. Payload contains `{ value, previousValue }`; context provides `signal`. Synchronous void waits for done; true, done(), or fulfilled `Promise<void>` allows saving. False, done(false), `Promise<false>`, throwing, or rejection cancels. Ordinary events only notify and do not await Promises; the DOM source of `change` may be absent.

### Textarea Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:modelValue | Model update proposal during input, clearing, or confirmed saving | `value: string \| null` |
| update:open | Editor visibility request | `open: boolean` |
| open-change | Editor visibility change notification | `open: boolean` |
| input | Length-normalized user input, emitted after composition completes | `value: string, event: Event` |
| change | Commit on blur, clear, or deferred saving; the source event is optional | `value: string \| null, event?: Event` |
| keydown | Native keyboard notification; Enter keeps its newline behavior in direct mode | `event: KeyboardEvent` |
| clear | Clear request, followed by input, model update, and change notifications | `event: Event` |
| focus | Native editor receives focus | `event: FocusEvent` |
| blur | Native editor loses focus | `event: FocusEvent` |

### Textarea Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read | Reading content with the raw value and formatted text | `{ value: string \| null; text: string }` |
| prefix | Prefix content | `-` |
| suffix | Suffix content | `-` |
| clear-icon | Clear icon or button | `{ clear(event?: Event): void }` |

### Textarea Methods

| Method | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| focus | Focus the mounted editor | `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void` |
| blur | Blur the mounted editor | `blur(): void` |
| select | Select all text in the mounted editor | `select(): void` |
| textareaRef | Reference to the mounted native textarea | `HTMLTextAreaElement \| undefined` |

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

Deferred `change` preserves the real confirmation event when available (for example, the save button). Programmatic editor handoff has no DOM event, so its second argument is optional. The event target can be the confirmation control rather than the input. `change` is a notification: its returned Promise is not awaited; use `before-commit` to approve asynchronous saves.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

# Theme Customization

Start with a built-in theme, then override the CSS variables you need. Themes control colors, corners and fonts. Use [SafeArea](#/en-US/safe-area) for device-edge spacing.

One theme boundary for the entire application or a subtree. A provider around the application is its global theme; nesting creates local overrides with the same rules. Providers never mutate html or other application roots.

## Choose an approach

| Goal | Recommended approach |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| One brand across the app | `<mp-theme-provider :theme="Themes.maple[mode]">` |
| Customize a region or component | `<mp-theme-provider :style-vars="…">` |
| Find supported overrides | The variable guide below and each component's CSS variable table |

## Brands and states

### Firefly button surfaces

Keep the existing status × variant API: yellow primary, neutral secondary and violet tertiary. Switch the card surface to compare transparent buttons, then inspect violet selection and focus across the related controls.

Example source: src/themes/example/FireflyScenes.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import { watchLang, watchTheme } from '@maple-design/cli-vue/client'
import { Themes } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'

const english = ref(false)
watchLang((value) => {
  english.value = value === 'en-US'
})
const mode = ref('light')
const background = ref('light')
watchTheme((theme) => {
  mode.value = theme.toLowerCase().includes('dark') ? 'dark' : 'light'
  background.value = mode.value === 'dark' ? 'navy' : 'light'
})
const variants = ['default', 'text', 'outline', 'tonal']

  { status: 'primary', label: '黄色主行动', labelEn: 'Yellow primary action' },

const agreement = ref(true)
const reminder = ref(true)

</script>
```

```vue
<mp-theme-provider :theme="mode">
  <App />
  <mp-theme-provider theme="light"><Preview /></mp-theme-provider>
</mp-theme-provider>
```

Omit theme to inherit. Use light/dark or a Themes preset object for an explicit boundary. Explicit themes replace inherited presets while style-vars overrides continue to inherit. style-vars overrides defaults, inner keys win, and null clears this layer. Explicit boundaries re-evaluate loaded component aliases. tag changes the wrapper; use a suitable layout host or display: contents where necessary.

Library declarative popups inherit their owning Vue provider with body, custom popup-container and inline targets. Services created outside a provider need a popup-container inside the themed region. Third-party Teleports need an explicit theme host; foreign documents must load the library styles.

## Application usage

### 1. Choose a built-in theme

| Code Theme | Light | Dark | Style |
| ------- | ---------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Default | `Themes.default.light` | `Themes.default.dark` | Teal |
| Maple | `Themes.maple.light` | `Themes.maple.dark` | Red-orange |
| Alps | `Themes.alps.light` | `Themes.alps.dark` | Dark primary buttons and orange selection controls |
| Firefly | `Themes.firefly.light` | `Themes.firefly.dark` | Yellow-green primary buttons, dark-blue text and rounded fields |

Alps/Firefly light themes follow brand styling; dark themes are Maple adaptations. Business code loads brand fonts; system fallback applies otherwise.


#### Firefly color roles and existing APIs

| Purpose | Maple usage | Horo role |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Yellow solid primary action | `status="primary" variant="default"` | primary |
| Neutral secondary action | `status="secondary"` | secondary |
| Purple auxiliary solid action | `status="tertiary" variant="default"` | tertiary; Firefly only |
| Purple text action | `status="tertiary" variant="text"` | text |
| Neutral text action | `status="default" variant="text"` | text_secondary |
| Yellow text on dark surfaces | `status="primary" variant="text"` | text_bg |

Yellow primary stays `#EAFF68`. Auxiliary purple fill uses `#CFC7FF`; light-mode text uses `#9A89EB`. secondary is neutral, not purple. text/outline stay transparent without extra supporting button backgrounds. Examples compare whole-card backgrounds. Raw light text does not guarantee contrast on every light background.

Selection, focus, sliders, date ranges and emphasized links use auxiliary purple. Body/general emphasis retain readable dark text adaptation. tonal/dark are Maple extensions of existing APIs, not claims of original Horo dark samples.

### 2. Set page background/text

Configure component themes together with business page backgrounds. Apply these styles to the element inside ThemeProvider that wraps the page:

```css
.app-page {
  color: var(--mp-color-text);
  background-color: var(--mp-color-body);
  color-scheme: var(--mp-color-scheme);
}
```

### 3. Override theme variables

Extend an existing theme, using corresponding bases for light/dark. The following adjusts only button corners:

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { Themes } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
const mode = ref('dark')
</script>
<template>
  <mp-theme-provider :theme="Themes.maple[mode]" :style-vars="{ '--mp-button-border-radius': '12px' }">
    <App />
  </mp-theme-provider>
</template>
```

## Unit conversion

`Themes.toRem(theme, { rootFontSize, unitPrecision })` and `Themes.toViewport(theme, { viewportWidth, viewportUnit, unitPrecision })` return new objects. The defaults are 16px and 375px respectively, precision 6, and viewport unit `vmin`. The reference size must be finite and positive, precision an integer from 0 to 100, and the unit a CSS viewport unit. Invalid options throw `RangeError`.

`Themes.convert(theme, converter)` replaces `px` numbers in values as text. The callback receives a signed numeric string and returns the replacement. This is not a CSS parser: matching text in strings and URLs is also replaced, so pass only dimension variables suitable for conversion.

## Finding variables

| Stack level | Example | Use case |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Brand palette steps | `--mp-primary-1` … `--mp-primary-10` | Build a complete brand palette with RGB-channel values |
| Semantic roles | `--mp-sys-color-content-primary`、`--mp-sys-color-surface-page` | General business text/page backgrounds |
| Component variables | `--mp-button-primary-color`、`--mp-button-border-radius` | Target a particular component |

Use RGB channels through `rgb(var(--mp-primary-6))`. Use complete color/dimension values as documented. `--mp-sys-font-family` is the font entry; applications supply font files.

See [Design Token layers](#/en-US/design-tokens) and component style-variable tables. For form interaction, see [Form](#/en-US/form).

## Installation and defaults

```ts
import { ThemeProvider } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
app.use(ThemeProvider)
ThemeProvider.setPropsDefaults({ theme: 'light', tag: 'section', styleVars: () => ({}) })
```

Defaults apply to subsequently created instances; explicit props take precedence. Variable objects are copied for each instance. SSR renders the same theme boundary as the client, without retaining theme state across requests.

## API

### ThemeProvider Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| theme | Light/dark mode or preset; inherit when omitted | `ThemeProviderTheme` | — |
| style-vars | CSS variables for this boundary; null clears the overrides | `StyleVars \| null` | `{}` |
| tag | Wrapper element tag | `string` | `'div'` |

The default slot supplies component content. No events.

## Types

Exports ThemeProvider, themeProviderProps, ThemeProviderProps, ThemeProviderInstance, ThemeProviderDefaults, ThemeProviderTheme, ThemeProviderMode, StyleVarName and StyleVars. Variables accept full --mp- names or camelCase names with the library prefix; values are CSS strings and dimensions require units.

Internal custom properties and measurement values are implementation details and are not customization APIs.

# TimeRange

## Basic examples

### 24hr And Seconds

```html
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref([])

```

### Next Day Label

When the end time is earlier than the start, `show-next-day` treats the end as the next day and shows a next-day marker. Without it, the draft is preserved, a red footer message is shown and confirmation is disabled. Now always updates only the active endpoint.

```html
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref(['22:00', '06:00'])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-time-range format="HH:mm" v-model="range" show-next-day placeholder="Overnight range" clearable />
</template>
```

## Appearance and presentation

### Field appearance and nested options

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `format` | String parse, display and output format | Field appearance and nested options, Range formats and 12-hour clocks, Visible wheel fields |
| `placeholder` | Endpoint placeholders; a string labels both endpoints | Field appearance and nested options, Range formats and 12-hour clocks, separator |
| `clearable` | Whether the value can be cleared | Range formats and 12-hour clocks, separator, next day |
| `separator` | Display separator | Field appearance and nested options, separator |
| `show-next-day` | Allow end before start as next day. Otherwise reversed drafts show a red warning and disable confirmation. Endpoints never swap | Range formats and 12-hour clocks, next day |
| `variant` | Variant: `filled` `standard` `outline` | Field appearance and nested options |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


hint controls the floating label (Cedar defaults to false, Maple to true) and is suppressed by an outer Form label. line defaults to true; text-color/focus-color/blur-color accept optional color strings. An unset error inherits Form state; explicit false overrides it. TimeRange separator defaults to `~` and accepts an empty string. Default variants remain Cedar filled and Maple standard; set variant explicitly for matching appearance.

The field owns values, defaults, open state, format, steps, bounds, disabled rules and readonly/disabled state. Set these directly on the field, not inside timeRangePickerProps. Nested options customize presentation only; model/select/confirm listeners cannot replace the field flow. Types reject owner properties and runtime filtering removes them, even when a top-level constraint is unset.

Maple pickerProps accepts visual options such as optionHeight/optionCount, not columns, fieldNames, selection, toolbar or open state. popupProps accepts positioning, appearance and lifecycle callbacks, but not open/defaultOpen or open-update listeners. Top-level popupContainer (including false) takes priority. Nested options in standalone time panels follow the same ownership rules.

Example source: src/time-range/example/demos/en-US/field-appearance.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref(['09:00', '18:00'])
const hint = ref(true)
const error = ref(false)
const line = ref(true)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="hint">Floating hint</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="error">Explicit error state</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="line">Border / underline</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-time-range
      v-model="value"
      format="HH:mm"
      variant="outline"
      :placeholder="['Start time', 'End time']"
      :hint="hint"
      :error="error"
      :line="line"
      focus-color="#6750a4"
      separator=" → "
    />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Field interactions use one local controller: select stages a draft; confirmation validates current rules before commit and Form change notification. Clearing uses the commit path with undefined, followed by clear; it is blocked when readonly/disabled or not clearable. Readonly fields remain focusable; repeated focus/blur notifications are deduplicated. A pending controlled close request cannot repeat a commit.

The panel owns one draft and confirmation flow; presentation content only renders that state. The example above counts valid confirmations and shows the extra slot. Reconfirming an unchanged value emits confirm without an extra change event.

```vue
</style>
```

The demo enables text entry and shows the model, preserving 22:00→next-day06:00 endpoint order. Clearing returns `undefined`; Reset restores the range. `show-next-day` describes clock ordering and the label, not automatic next-day calendar arithmetic.

## Value model and selection rules

### Model types and literals

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `format` | String parse, display and output format | Model types and literals, Hour/minute/second steps, Time bounds |
| `min` | Minimum selectable time | Time bounds, Wheel constraints |
| `max` | Maximum selectable time | Time bounds, Wheel constraints |
| `presentation` | Panel mode: `picker` | Hour/minute/second steps |

### Hour/minute/second steps

Example source: src/time-range/example/demos/en-US/step.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref(['09:30:00', '17:00:00'])
const step = { hour: 1, minute: 15, second: 10 }
const use12Hours = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <p>Hourly candidates, 15-minute and 10-second intervals.</p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="use12Hours">12-hour panel; model remains HH:mm:ss</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-time-range
      v-model="value"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      :use12-hours="use12Hours"
      :step="step"
      style="width: 100%; max-width: 360px"
    />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Switch to a 12-hour panel without changing minute/second intervals. The explicit `HH:mm:ss` format still controls the model; AM/PM choices map to the corresponding 24-hour value.

`format` it parses string models and controls display and emitted strings. The default is `HH:mm:ss`; with `use12-hours` and no explicit format it is `hh:mm:ss a`. Use `HH:mm` to serialize minutes, and time-fields to hide wheel seconds, `hh:mm A` for uppercase AM/PM, and `[Time] HH:mm` for literal text. Models accept formatted strings, local Date objects, or millisecond timestamps; output is always a formatted string (an array for ranges). Invalid input is not normalized or written back. `min`/`max` remain 24-hour `HH:mm[:ss]` strings, and disabled callbacks always receive actual hours 0–23.

### Time bounds

`min` / `max` are optional strings, with no bound by default. Use 24-hour `HH:mm` or `HH:mm:ss`, independently of format/use12Hours. Both endpoints are inclusive; omitted seconds mean 00. Range endpoints are validated individually; showNextDay does not make the bounds wrap across midnight. Reversed bounds allow no commit; unparseable bounds are treated as unset.

Changing bounds does not rewrite the external model. Commits must satisfy bounds, steps and disabled callbacks. Hidden seconds are validated as 00. Coarse list columns are disabled when their whole hour/minute is out of bounds; confirmation validates the complete time. Use hide-disabled-options to hide disabled choices.

Example source: src/time-range/example/demos/en-US/bounds.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref(['10:30:38', '10:31:02'])
const narrow = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <p>
      Inclusive bounds: 10:30:38–10:31:02. Narrowing the bounds preserves the current model but prevents invalid
      confirmation.
    </p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="narrow">Move minimum to 10:30:40</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-time-range
      v-model="value"
      input-editable
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      :min="narrow ? '10:30:40' : '10:30:38'"
      max="10:31:02"
    />
    <mp-time-range-picker v-model="value" format="HH:mm:ss" :min="narrow ? '10:30:40' : '10:30:38'" max="10:31:02" />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Toggling readonly, hiding disabled options, or enabling `disable-confirm` does not commit an existing draft. Unlocking also leaves the model unchanged. With immediate mode enabled, the next valid user selection commits. Readonly preserves the current draft; hiding forbidden options changes candidate visibility, not the committed value.

Switching Maple between wheels preserves both draft endpoints and the active endpoint without confirming. Readonly remains effective after switching. An external model replacement updates either presentation instead of retaining the old draft.

The standalone panel owns its draft and commit state directly. External model replacement resets the draft without emitting selection or change events. Read-only and disabled states block selection and confirmation. Cedar renders lists; Maple renders wheels. These views do not create a second draft.

#### disabled

Disabled callbacks match Cedar: disabled-hours, disabled-minutes and disabled-seconds. Both views respect inclusive same-day min/max. Overnight ranges use show-next-day. ### Text entry

`input-editable` defaults to `false` (Cedar: `true`). When enabled, tap the input to type; use the clock button or ArrowDown to open the picker panel. Enter or blur commits; Escape cancels. Parsing, steps, bounds and disabled rules match panel selection. Invalid or rejected controlled edits restore the model value. Disabling editing, readonly or disabled state discards drafts. IME composition and moving between range inputs do not commit.

Example source: src/time-range/example/demos/en-US/text-entry.vue

### Intro

Form time-range **field**. Cancel discards the draft; Confirm writes `v-model`.

The popup uses [`TimeRangePicker`](en-US/time-range-picker) as the panel. Top summaries are omitted; paired wheels edit start (left) and end (right) together.

- Uses column wheels by default (hour / minute / second)

### Default and controlled values

`defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled fields/panels once; subsequent edits are retained locally. `modelValue` is authoritative when provided. `defaultOpen` initializes field visibility once. Controlled `open` requires the parent to accept `update:open`; `open-change(open: boolean)` reports requests. `clear` has no arguments. Panels support `disabled` for both range endpoints.

Example source: src/time-range/example/demos/en-US/default-state.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref(['09:00', '10:00'])
const open = ref(false)
const acceptValue = ref(true)
const acceptOpen = ref(true)
const acceptClose = ref(true)
const commits = ref(0)
const proposal = ref()
const openProposal = ref()
const updateValue = (next) => {
  proposal.value = next
  if (acceptValue.value) {
    value.value = next
  }
}
const updateOpen = (next) => {
  openProposal.value = next
  if (acceptOpen.value && (next || acceptClose.value)) {
    open.value = next
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="12px" style="width: 100%">
    <p>Uncontrolled initial value</p>
    <mp-time-range :default-value="['09:00', '10:00']" format="HH:mm" clearable />
    <p>Controlled value and visibility</p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="acceptValue">Accept value updates</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="acceptOpen">Accept visibility updates</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-time-range
      :model-value="value"
      :open="open"
      format="HH:mm"
      clearable
      @update:model-value="updateValue"
      @update:open="updateOpen"
      @change="commits++"
    />
    <span>{{ value }} / {{ open }}</span>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="acceptClose">Accept close requests</mp-checkbox>
    <output aria-label="Commit count">{{ commits }}</output>
    <output aria-label="Controlled proposals">{{ JSON.stringify({ value: proposal, open: openProposal }) }}</output>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Use the acceptance switches to reject value or visibility requests independently. Rejected requests leave parent state unchanged; proposals are shown separately. Reopening restores the parent model. A close request does not imply parent acceptance.

When the parent rejects closing, repeated confirmation without a new selection does not commit again. A fresh time selection starts a new transaction that can be confirmed while the panel remains open.

### Selection and commit

Field `focus` and `blur` events have no arguments and fire once per transition. Moving between range endpoints stays within one field. Readonly fields remain focusable but cannot open for editing; disabling a focused field releases its focus state and notifies blur.

Fields and standalone panels revalidate the current format, steps and disabled rules at commit time. Cedar text input follows the same rules. Changing constraints does not rewrite committed values. Reversed ranges are accepted only when `show-next-day` is enabled; otherwise a red footer message is shown and confirmation is disabled. Endpoints are never swapped. Clearing commits `undefined` regardless of candidate restrictions, but still respects readonly/disabled state.

`select(value, date)` reports user draft selection; `change(value, date)` reports a committed value. Both single and range fields clear to `undefined`, with an undefined date argument and a no-argument `clear` event. Date arguments represent local clock times (not next-day calendar arithmetic). Fields default to explicit confirmation; `disable-confirm` commits a valid choice immediately and requests close. Range confirmation rejects reversed endpoints unless `show-next-day` is enabled. Controlled `open` still requires parent acceptance. Standalone panels also default to confirmation; disable-confirm commits immediately without closing the panel.

Example source: src/time-range/example/demos/en-US/selection-events.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref(['09:00', '18:00'])
const immediate = ref(false)
const readonly = ref(false)
const disabled = ref(false)
const events = ref([])
function record(name, value, dates) {
  const times = Array.isArray(dates) ? dates.map((date) => date?.toLocaleTimeString()) : dates?.toLocaleTimeString()
  events.value = [JSON.stringify({ event: name, value: value ?? null, time: times ?? null }), ...events.value].slice(
    0,
    5,
  )
}
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="12px" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="readonly">Read-only: focus allowed, edits blocked</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="disabled">Disabled: focus released, edits blocked</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="immediate">Commit immediately on selection</mp-checkbox>
    <p>Select records drafts. Change records commits. Cancel leaves the model unchanged. Clear returns undefined.</p>
    <mp-time-range
      v-model="value"
      :disable-confirm="immediate"
      :readonly="readonly"
      :disabled="disabled"
      format="HH:mm"
      clearable
      @select="(value, dates) => record('select', value, dates)"
      @change="(value, dates) => record('change', value, dates)"
      @clear="record('clear')"
      @click="record('click')"
      @open-change="(open) => record('open-change', open)"
      @focus="record('focus')"
      @blur="record('blur')"
    />
    <span>Model: {{ value === undefined ? 'undefined' : value }}</span>
    <mp-button variant="outline" @click="value = ['15:30', '18:00']">Replace model externally</mp-button>
    <small>External replacement updates the display without emitting select or change.</small>
    <div v-for="(event, index) in events" :key="index" style="overflow-wrap: anywhere">{{ event }}</div>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Replacing the model from the parent resets the draft without emitting `select` or `change`. The example includes an external-update button; confirming a user selection remains a separate action.

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Reading direction

Range values stay `[start, end]`. LTR/RTL changes affect layout without swapping endpoints or changing cross-day meaning. Time columns and start/end panels follow reading order. Left/Right moves focus visually, including across endpoints. Cedar Up/Down moves focus and Enter/Space selects; Maple Up/Down retains wheel selection semantics. Existing draft/confirmation configuration is preserved, and popovers inherit source field direction.

## Usage notes

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `popup` and opens an editor when the value area is clicked. Supported values: `direct / popup`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Maple uses edit-mode="popup" to open the editor when the value area is clicked; direct edits immediately. readPretty is a reading-only setting, independent of readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

Inline date/time fields retain existing confirmation policies. In popover/popup, pure panels hide confirmation tools and the editor provides one confirm/cancel pair. Standalone DatePicker/DateRangePicker/TimePicker/TimeRangePicker retain panel APIs/confirmation without inheriting Form field presentation.

Mobile date fields use `panel-type` to select calendar/wheel content; `edit-mode` controls only field editing. Standalone panel content follows each panel API and is not controlled by the field `edit-mode`.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

### Panel actions

Headers follow hour/minute/second format and align with both wheel groups; 12-hour mode adds AM/PM. No top summary or visible endpoint labels appear. Left edits start, right edits end; cross-day status appears below the right group.

Shared style variables:


Range panels provide Now by default. Start is initially current; using the right wheel makes end current. Now changes only that endpoint's draft. Even with `disable-confirm`, Now/subsequent edits require confirmation; cancel discards them. Format/step/disabling rules apply, and next-day/order checks update immediately. Fields, independent panels and popups behave alike; top-level `:show-now-button="false"` hides it. Custom `actions` can use `selectNow()`/`nowDisabled`.

### Forwarded configuration boundaries

The time field manages open/defaultOpen, disabled, trigger, closeOnClickReference, preventFocus and visibility updates. An explicit top-level popup-container takes precedence over nested configuration; popupClass is merged. Inline presentation fixes popupOffset=4, and Maple also fixes unmountOnClose=true, so those nested fields may not control the final values.

### Configuration

See [`TimeRangePicker`](#/en-US/time-range-picker) for panel style variables.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](#/en-US/emptyValues).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

`popup-props` configures the anchored Trigger popover on both platforms. It cannot replace field open/disabled/trigger ownership. Top-level popup-container, including false, takes precedence. Panel and popup options are separate. `click(event)` fires once for an enabled field; readonly fields notify but do not open. Use `open-change(false)` for close requests, not proof that a controlled state changed. 

`suffix-icon` receives `focus: boolean` and `popupOpen: boolean`, replacing arrow-icon. `focus(index = 0)` focuses start (0) or end (1) without committing; `blur()` removes focus and requests closing.

Range `placeholder` accepts `string | string[]`: a string labels both endpoints; array entries label each endpoint, with missing entries empty. Explicit empty strings do not fall back to defaults.

### Pure-panel event and slot boundaries

`TimePicker`/`TimeRangePicker` do not manage fields/popups. Pass `open`, `size`, `variant`, clearing and popup configuration to `Time`/`TimeRange`.

- `select(value, date)`: edit the draft.
- `change(value, date)`: valid confirmation with a changed value; updates the model.
- `confirm(value, date)`: every valid confirmation, including unchanged values. `disableConfirm` also emits it on valid selection commits. Disabled, readonly or invalid drafts do not emit it.
- `extra`: additional explanatory content.
- `actions({ confirm, canConfirm, value })`: replace default tools. `value` is the draft; call `confirm()` to commit and disable buttons according to `canConfirm`.

Single-time events carry formatted strings and Date objects; range events carry corresponding arrays. Use field `open-change` and `update:open` to manage the popup, and field `clear` for clearing the value.

Panels edit a draft and commit on confirmation. Cancellation or closing does not commit, while clearing commits an empty value and closes immediately. Mobile time fields do not open the software keyboard. See the combined field examples in the Date documentation.

### TimeRange Props

`input-attrs` applies to the two direct input elements. For example, `:input-attrs="[{ 'aria-label': 'Departure' }, { 'aria-label': 'Return' }]"` names each endpoint. The field owns its value, disabled, readonly, placeholder, role and popup state; shared descriptions, per-input descriptions and form errors are merged for each input. Component errors take precedence; otherwise each input retains its `aria-invalid`. `RangeInputAttributes` is exported from the component and root entries and includes native attributes and `Once` event types.

When FormItem `label-attrs.for` explicitly targets one endpoint, each otherwise unnamed endpoint uses the form label and a localized start or end name. Explicit accessible names on `input-attrs` or the field take precedence. Older custom locales can provide `fieldPresentation.rangeStart` and `fieldPresentation.rangeEnd`; otherwise the existing date or time endpoint text is used.

### Disabling rules

Clock/wheels share three callbacks returning disabled-value arrays; hours always use 0–23. Hours/minutes without valid descendants are omitted from wheels.

## TimeRangePicker range panel

Installing TimeRange also registers TimeRangePicker, which is available through the static member `TimeRange.Picker`.

### Introduction

A standalone embeddable time-range panel. It has no top summary; two wheel groups simultaneously edit start/end.

- Defaults to column wheels: hour/minute/second

Form field: [`TimeRange`](llms/en-US/time-range.md). Single time panel: [`TimePicker`](en-US/time-picker).

### Basic usage

```html
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref(['09:00', '18:00'])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-time-range-picker format="HH:mm" v-model="range" />
</template>
```

### 24-hour format and seconds

```html
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref(['09:00:00', '18:00:00'])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-time-range-picker format="HH:mm:ss" v-model="range" />
</template>
```

### Readonly

```html
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref(['09:00', '18:00'])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-time-range-picker format="HH:mm" v-model="range" readonly />
</template>
```

### Next-day marker

```html
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref(['22:00', '06:00'])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-time-range-picker format="HH:mm" v-model="range" show-next-day />
</template>
```

With `show-next-day`, an earlier end is next day and marked accordingly. Otherwise a bottom red warning disables confirmation. Selection/confirmation never swap endpoints; Now updates only the current endpoint.

### Actions

```html
<script setup>
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref(['09:00', '18:00'])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-time-range-picker format="HH:mm" v-model="range">
    <template #actions="{ confirm, canConfirm }">
      <mp-button status="primary" variant="text" :disabled="!canConfirm" @click="confirm">Confirm</mp-button>
    </template>
  </mp-time-range-picker>
</template>
```

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

## Visible wheel fields

`time-fields` controls time-wheel visibility/order, shared by both endpoints and by fields/independent panels.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `time-fields` | readonly TimePickerField[]<br>`TimePickerField: 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | Generated from the time-format protocol | Controls time wheels, including those embedded in calendars. |

Arrays must be nonempty and unique; explicit arrays strictly determine column visibility/order. Omission uses defaults. Date/time field groups validate separately and cannot mix. Hidden units retain existing values and merge back into the complete draft. Changing field configuration does not commit the model. Nested display options cannot override root props.

Time/TimeRange format retains parsing/display/output semantics. time-fields controls panel columns only. Hidden units already in the model retain their values. 12-hour mode adds AM/PM automatically when hour is visible.

```vue
../../time/example/demos/time-fields.vue
```

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

During deferred editing, clearing retains the configured valid empty-value and confirmation submits that empty value; null is not replaced by midnight. A newly created empty wheel panel may initialize a visible candidate without selecting or committing a model. Later explicit empty drafts in that panel are not automatically refilled. Reopening and cancelling does not publish another value.

### Field notifications and public types

Field update:modelValue/change use TimeModelValue (TimeRangeModelValue for ranges). Normal selections commit formatted strings; explicit clears retain configured null, timestamps, Date objects or range arrays accepted by the property. Auxiliary dates may be undefined; clearing a range to an empty array also yields an empty auxiliary array. Clear does not emit select. Select remains a formatted user draft, which may be incomplete for a range.

Exports TimeEmits, TimeModelValue, TimeReadScope, TimeSuffixIconScope, TimeSlots, TimeActionsScope and TimeExpose, plus TimeRangeEmits, TimeRangeModelValue, TimeRangeReadScope, TimeRangeSlots, TimeRangeActionsScope and TimeRangeExpose. Import each from the root or its component entry. Instances include the public Expose contract.

Field read receives { value, text } with a nullable model; suffix-icon receives { focus, popupOpen }; clear-icon receives a guarded clear(event?). Range fields also support separator. Cedar direct mode supports a default custom trigger, while Maple does not. Neither platform currently forwards field loading-icon, so types do not promise it. actions/extra operate on panel drafts: Cedar forwards them in direct mode; Maple forwards them during deferred editing, not direct mode. Inner confirm is not the outer final-save entry.


<!-- time-contract:start -->

### Defaults and format

Inherited, format-derived and effective-step defaults describe resolved behavior; raw Props may be undefined. Without format, the default is HH:mm:ss, or hh:mm:ss a with use12Hours=true. Bounds use 24-hour clock times, separate from Date-family valueFormat/time-zone rules.

### Field event and slot parameter types

Events notify only; listener Promises are not collected. update:modelValue and change include null, 0, Date or range arrays allowed by the clearing policy. select reports formatted draft rather than saving. Field update:open/open-change are opening requests; initialization does not notify automatically.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TimeRangeModelValue` |
| `change` | `TimeRangeModelValue, (Date \| undefined)[] \| undefined` |
| `select` | `(string \| undefined)[] \| undefined, (Date \| undefined)[] \| undefined` |
| `clear` | `()` |
| `click` | `Event` |
| `focus` | `()` |
| `blur` | `()` |
| `update:open` | `boolean` |
| `open-change` | `boolean` |

Field focus(index?)/blur() target the actual input or trigger without changing model. read receives value/text, suffix-icon receives focus/popupOpen, and clear-icon receives guarded clear(event?). prefix, selected, suffix and extra are unscoped; ranges also have separator. Cedar direct mode has a custom default trigger slot; Maple does not.

actions/extra belong to panel draft: Cedar direct forwards them, Maple direct does not, and deferred editing forwards them. Panel confirm() is not the outer field final-save entry point. Pure panels have actions/extra, without field read/clear-icon/loading-icon slots. Standalone panels expose no ref.confirm() method; custom confirmation uses actions.confirm.

### Panel event parameter types

Arguments are tuples from the corresponding public event type. Date arguments are parsed from formatted clock times and do not promise to preserve an input Date calendar day.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TimeRangePickerEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `TimeRangePickerEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `TimeRangePickerEmits['select']` |
| `confirm` | `TimeRangePickerEmits['confirm']` |

### Panel Events

Pure-panel business events are update:modelValue, change, select and confirm. select reports candidates; valid confirmation notifies confirm, while update:modelValue/change only occur for an actual value change. Field opening, clearing and focus events do not belong to pure panels.

Complete panel actions scope below; extra has no arguments.

```ts
import type { TimeValue } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
type PanelActionsScope = { confirm: () => boolean; canConfirm: boolean; value: Array<TimeValue | undefined> | undefined; selectNow: () => boolean; nowDisabled: boolean }
```

### Explicit save guard

beforeCommit(payload, done, context) belongs to field saving. payload contains value/previousValue; context has signal and optional event. Returning undefined waits for done, while boolean/Promise results settle by their result. FormItem validates candidates first; failure retains draft. Ordinary select/change/confirm/click listener returns do not use this task protocol.

### Type imports

```ts
import { TimeRange, TimeRangePicker, type TimeRangeProps, type TimeRangeEmits,
  type TimeRangeSlots, type TimeRangeInstance, type TimeRangePickerProps,
  type TimeRangePickerEmits, type TimeRangePickerSlots } from '@maple-design/ui-vue'
```

## CSS Variables

The following CSS variables support customization with [ThemeProvider](#/en-US/theme-provider).

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--mp-time-range-picker-background` | `var(--mp-sys-color-surface-overlay)` | `background`, `background-image` |
| `--mp-time-range-picker-border-radius` | `var(--mp-time-picker-border-radius, 4px)` | `border-radius` |
| `--mp-time-range-picker-column-label-height` | `var(--mp-internal-temporal-panel-column-label-height)` | `height` |
| `--mp-time-range-picker-next-day-color` | `var(--mp-sys-color-content-secondary)` | `color` |
| `--mp-time-range-title-font-size` | `var(--mp-picker-title-font-size, 16px)` | `font-size` |
| `--mp-time-range-title-text-color` | `var(--mp-picker-title-text-color, #555)` | `color` |
| `--mp-time-range-toolbar-height` | `var(--mp-picker-toolbar-height, 44px)` | `height` |
| `--mp-time-range-toolbar-padding` | `var(--mp-picker-toolbar-padding, 0 4px)` | `padding` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --mp-time-range-picker-background: var(--mp-sys-color-surface-overlay);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- Source: src/time/docs/en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en-US/time -->

# Time

If a parent keeps the popup open after confirmation, repeated confirmation without a new selection is deduplicated. A fresh time selection starts a new transaction and can be confirmed again.

While expanded, the native combobox uses `aria-controls` to identify its own named popup. Closing updates the state and removes the link. `aria-label` and `aria-describedby` reach the native input. Custom selected/trigger slots must preserve accessible names, keyboard operation and state associations.

In clock and wheel modes, min/max are inclusive same-day bounds. A minute stays selectable when some of its seconds are available. Second constraints compare the complete clock value, not seconds from a different hour. Use TimeRange show-next-day for overnight ranges, rather than reversed min/max.

Installing Time also registers TimePicker, which is available through the static member `Time.Picker`.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

```vue
  <mp-space direction="column" size="lg">
    <mp-time v-model="time" format="HH:mm" placeholder="Select a time" clearable />
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Compare Input, Button, Select, date/time fields and other single-line controls at the same size. Field variants share the height scale; Button uses outline here. DatePicker/TimePicker are panels; this example uses Date/Time fields. The example includes selected and clearable values, removable tags and long multiple selections. Select/Cascader keep the same size height with tag-nowrap. Long tag text uses ellipsis while removal icons remain available; tags scroll horizontally while clear and arrow controls stay outside the scrolling area. Hover, focus or tap truncated tag text to read its full content; dismiss with an outside click or Escape without changing the selected value. Restore values after clearing to repeat the comparison. Multiline text and wrapping multiple selections can grow with content.

### Field appearance and nested options

hint controls the floating label (Cedar defaults to false, Maple to true) and is suppressed by an outer Form label. line defaults to true; text-color/focus-color/blur-color accept optional color strings. An unset error inherits Form state; explicit false overrides it. TimeRange separator defaults to `~` and accepts an empty string. Default variants remain Cedar filled and Maple standard; set variant explicitly for matching appearance.

The field owns values, defaults, open state, format, steps, bounds, disabled rules and readonly/disabled state. Set these directly on the field, not inside timePickerProps/timeRangePickerProps. Nested options customize presentation only; model/select/confirm listeners cannot replace the field flow. Types reject owner properties and runtime filtering removes them, even when a top-level constraint is unset.

Maple pickerProps accepts visual options such as optionHeight/optionCount, not columns, fieldNames, selection, toolbar or open state. popupProps accepts positioning, appearance and lifecycle callbacks, but not open/defaultOpen or open-update listeners. Top-level popupContainer (including false) takes priority. Nested options in standalone time panels follow the same ownership rules.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/field-appearance.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:00')
const hint = ref(true)
const error = ref(false)
const line = ref(true)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="hint">Floating hint</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="error">Explicit error state</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="line">Border / underline</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-time
      v-model="value"
      format="HH:mm"
      variant="outline"
      placeholder="Choose time"
      :hint="hint"
      :error="error"
      :line="line"
      focus-color="#6750a4"
    />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

Field interactions use one local controller: select stages a draft; confirmation validates current rules before commit and Form change notification. Clearing uses the commit path with undefined, followed by clear; it is blocked when readonly/disabled or not clearable. Readonly fields remain focusable; repeated focus/blur notifications are deduplicated. A pending controlled close request cannot repeat a commit.

The panel owns one draft and confirmation flow; presentation content only renders that state. The example above counts valid confirmations and shows the extra slot. Reconfirming an unchanged value emits confirm without an extra change event.

### Visible wheel fields

`time-fields` controls time columns and their order on fields and standalone panels. Range endpoints share the configuration.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `time-fields` | readonly TimePickerField[]<br>`TimePickerField: 'hour' \| 'minute' \| 'second'` | According to the time format | Controls time wheels, including those embedded in calendars. |

Lists must be nonempty and unique. Explicit lists determine columns and order; only omitted props use defaults. Date and time fields cannot be mixed. Edits preserve hidden units in the full draft. Changing fields does not submit the model. Nested presentation props cannot override root field configuration.

Time format retains its string parsing/display/output protocol. time-fields changes columns only and retains hidden units represented in the model. Twelve-hour hour columns automatically include AM/PM.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/time-fields.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import type { TimePickerField } from '../../picker-props'

const props = defineProps<{ range?: boolean; english?: boolean }>()
const preset = ref('hour-minute')
const fields = computed<TimePickerField[]>(() =>
  preset.value === 'minute-hour' ? ['minute', 'hour'] : preset.value === 'second' ? ['second'] : ['hour', 'minute'],
)
const time = ref('09:30:17')
const times = ref(['09:30:17', '18:00:23'])
</script>
<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" align="stretch">
    <mp-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" :label="english ? 'Visible wheel fields' : '滚轮可见字段'">
      <mp-radio-group
        v-model="preset"
        :aria-label="english ? 'Visible wheel fields' : '滚轮可见字段'"
        :options="[
          { label: english ? 'Hour / minute' : '时 / 分', value: 'hour-minute' },
          { label: english ? 'Minute / hour' : '分 / 时', value: 'minute-hour' },
          { label: english ? 'Second only' : '仅秒', value: 'second' },
        ]"
        variant="button"
        size="sm"
      />
    </mp-form-item>
    <mp-time-range v-if="props.range" v-model="times" :time-fields="fields" format="HH:mm:ss" />
    <mp-time v-else v-model="time" :time-fields="fields" format="HH:mm:ss" />
    <p>{{ english ? 'Hidden fields retain their values:' : '隐藏字段保留原值：' }} {{ props.range ? times : time }}</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `format` | String parse, display and output format | Model types and literals, Hour/minute/second steps, Time bounds |

### Hour/minute/second steps

With 12-hour display and a 5-hour step, hours remain anchored to midnight: 0/5/10/15/20, not restarted at noon. AM offers 12/05/10 and PM offers 03/08. Selecting 03 PM commits 15:30:00 because this Demo retains HH:mm:ss as its model format. Changing the rules preserves the old 09:30:00; cancellation does not commit aligned candidates. Only confirmation writes the selected value. Enable Disable 15:00 to combine disabled-hours with the step: 03 PM is unavailable while 08 PM still means 20:00. Turning off Accept controlled updates records proposals without changing the business value; re-enable it before confirming an accepted value. Proposal counts are not acceptance counts. Other non-dividing steps and physical touch remain separate coverage.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/step.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:30:00')
const coarse = ref(false)
const fiveHours = ref(false)
const blockAfternoon = ref(false)
const accept = ref(true)
const proposals = ref(0)
const disabledHours = () => (blockAfternoon.value ? [15] : [])
function update(next) {
  proposals.value++
  if (accept.value) {
    value.value = next
  }
}
const step = computed(() => ({ hour: fiveHours.value ? 5 : 1, minute: coarse.value ? 30 : 15, second: 10 }))
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space class="time-step-demo" direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="fiveHours">12-hour display with a 5-hour step</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="coarse">Use 30-minute intervals</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="blockAfternoon">Disable 15:00 (03 PM)</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="accept">Accept controlled updates</mp-checkbox>
    <p>Confirmation validates the current step. Changing a rule does not change the committed value.</p>
    <mp-time
      :model-value="value"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      :use12-hours="fiveHours"
      :step="step"
      :disabled-hours="disabledHours"
      style="width: 100%; max-width: 360px"
      @update:model-value="update"
    />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
    <span role="status">Proposals：{{ proposals }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Time bounds

After tightening the minimum to 10:30:40, the field retains 10:30:38 but the panel cannot confirm it. Selecting and confirming the inclusive maximum 10:31:02 updates the model. Editing seconds to 00 and canceling keeps seconds 02.

`min` / `max` are optional strings, with no bound by default. Use 24-hour `HH:mm` or `HH:mm:ss`, independently of format/use12Hours. Both endpoints are inclusive; omitted seconds mean 00. Range endpoints are validated individually; showNextDay does not make the bounds wrap across midnight. Reversed bounds allow no commit; unparseable bounds are treated as unset.

Changing bounds does not rewrite the external model. Commits must satisfy bounds, steps and disabled callbacks. Hidden seconds are validated as 00. Coarse list columns are disabled when their whole hour/minute is out of bounds; confirmation validates the complete time. Use hide-disabled-options to hide disabled choices.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/bounds.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('10:30:38')
const narrow = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <p>
      Inclusive bounds: 10:30:38–10:31:02. Narrowing the bounds preserves the current model but prevents invalid
      confirmation.
    </p>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="narrow">Move minimum to 10:30:40</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-time v-model="value" format="HH:mm:ss" :min="narrow ? '10:30:40' : '10:30:38'" max="10:31:02" />
    <mp-time-picker v-model="value" format="HH:mm:ss" :min="narrow ? '10:30:40' : '10:30:38'" max="10:31:02" />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

### Wheel constraints

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/wheel-limits.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('10:30:40')
const locked = ref(false)
const disabledHours = () => (locked.value ? Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, hour) => hour) : [])
const disabledMinutes = (hour) => (hour === 10 ? [45] : [])
const disabledSeconds = (hour, minute) => (hour === 10 && minute === 30 ? [41, 43, 45] : [])
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" :size="12" style="width: 100%">
    <p>
      Inclusive 10:30:38–11:30:02. Change the hour to see dependent minutes and seconds; blocking all hours prevents
      confirmation.
    </p>
    <mp-button @click="locked = !locked">{{ locked ? 'Restore choices' : 'Block all hours' }}</mp-button>
    <mp-time
      v-model="value"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      panel-type="picker"
      min="10:30:38"
      max="11:30:02"
      :disabled-hours="disabledHours"
      :disabled-minutes="disabledMinutes"
      :disabled-seconds="disabledSeconds"
    />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

## Standalone time panels

### Basic Usage


### Panel confirmation and disabled options

For a pending single-value draft, enabling readonly, hiding disabled hours or switching to immediate mode does not submit the old draft. Unlocking does not submit it either; the next valid selection commits once. Maple wheel updates preserve the same draft without updating the parent model. Mouse/keyboard checks do not establish physical touch-inertia behavior.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/panel-behavior.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('09:30')
const immediate = ref(false)
const confirmations = ref(0)
const hideDisabled = ref(false)
const readonly = ref(false)
const disabledHours = () => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
</script>

<template>
  <mp-space direction="column" size="12px" style="width: 100%">
    <mp-checkbox v-model="immediate">Commit without confirmation</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="hideDisabled">Hide disabled hours (00–07)</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-checkbox v-model="readonly">Read-only (including confirmation)</mp-checkbox>
    <mp-button variant="outline" @click="value = '13:45'">Replace externally with 13:45</mp-button>
    <mp-time-picker
      v-model="value"
      format="HH:mm"
      :disable-confirm="immediate"
      :hide-disabled-options="hideDisabled"
      :readonly="readonly"
      :disabled-hours="disabledHours"
      @confirm="confirmations++"
    >
      <template #extra><p>Changing presentation keeps the draft; extra content uses the same slot.</p></template>
    </mp-time-picker>
    <span>Valid confirmations: {{ confirmations }}</span>
    <span>Committed value: {{ value }}</span>
    <p>With confirmation enabled, selection only changes the draft. The value above changes after confirmation.</p>
  </mp-space>
</template>
```

The standalone panel owns its draft and commit state directly. External model replacement resets the draft without emitting selection or change events. Read-only and disabled states block selection and confirmation. Cedar renders lists; Maple renders wheels. These views do not create a second draft.

## Input and state control

### Interaction state comparison

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `format` | String parse, display and output format | Interaction state comparison, Text entry, Default and controlled values |
| `clearable` | Whether the value can be cleared | Text entry, Default and controlled values, Selection and commit |
| `readonly` | Whether readonly | Interaction state comparison, Selection and commit, Multiple independent fields |
| `disabled` | Whether disabled | Interaction state comparison, Selection and commit |
| `input-editable` | Allow text entry; panel selection remains available | Text entry, Copying and editing |
| `placeholder` | Placeholder | Multiple independent fields, With FormItem |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->

### Text entry

`input-editable` defaults to `false` (Cedar: `true`). When enabled, tap the input to type; use the clock button or ArrowDown to open the picker/clock panel. Enter or blur commits; Escape cancels. Parsing, steps, bounds and disabled rules match panel selection. Invalid or rejected controlled edits restore the model value. Disabling editing, readonly or disabled state discards drafts. IME composition and moving between range inputs do not commit.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/text-entry.vue

```vue
      the panel.
```

### Intro

Form time **field** that opens `TimePicker` in a bottom popup. Interaction matches Select picker mode: Cancel discards the draft; Confirm writes `v-model`.

For time ranges, use [`TimeRange`](llms/en-US/time-range.md). For panel-only, use [`TimePicker`](en-US/time-picker). For time range panel, use [`TimeRangePicker`](en-US/time-range-picker).

### Default and controlled values

`defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled fields/panels once; subsequent edits are retained locally. `modelValue` is authoritative when provided. `defaultOpen` initializes field visibility once. Controlled `open` requires the parent to accept `update:open`; `open-change(open: boolean)` reports requests. `clear` has no arguments. Panels support `disabled` for both range endpoints.

Example source: src/time/example/demos/en-US/default-state.vue

```vue

const open = ref(false)
</script>
```
